# kratos-admin

`kratos-admin` is a management system warehouse with separate front-end and back-end, including Go + Kratos backend, Vue management backend, uni-app application base, React/Taro application base, versioned database migration and module scaffolding.

## Implemented capabilities

- Account password, verification code, OAuth, JWT refresh, tenant and Casbin permissions.
- User, role, department, position, menu, dictionary, configuration, task, log, region, API and migration record management.
- Proto-driven HTTP, gRPC, OpenAPI, Agent Tool, MCP Tool and TypeScript RPC generation.
- AI sessions, streaming messages, attachments, tool calls, retries, regenerations, and branching sessions.
- Manage side code generation configuration, preview, build progress and restore.
- Running log browsing: real-time console SSE, historical log query, level and keyword filtering and historical original file download.
- During the build period, README/docs of the current project, host project and external modules are collected and viewed uniformly on the management side.
- mountable Go Core module; the backend implements `module.Module`, provides static resources through `Resources`, and hands them to the Core unified registration protocol service from the startup entry.
- Language collections for admin, uni-app, Taro and backend error directories are automatically discovered by language packs; dynamic menus, dictionaries and code generation synchronization support all registered languages.

The warehouse does not include business modules such as mall, order, payment or recommendation.

## Table of Contents

| Table of Contents | Description | Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | Kratos services, Proto, GORM, migrations and Core hosting portfolio. | [backend/README.md](backend/README.md) |
| `frontend/admin` | Management workspace, including default host, core, System and CLI. | [frontend/admin/README.md](frontend/admin/README.md) |
| `frontend/uni-app` | uni-app workspace, including default host, core, system and CLI. | [frontend/uni-app/README.md](frontend/uni-app/README.md) |
| `frontend/taro-app` | React/Taro workspace, including default host, core, UI, system and CLI. | [frontend/taro-app/README.md](frontend/taro-app/README.md) |
| `docs` | Current structure, operating procedures and topic descriptions. | [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) |

## Environment

- Go `1.26.3`.
- Node.js `^20.19.0` or `>=22.12.0`.
- The pnpm version is subject to `packageManager` of each workspace: `10.33.4` on the management side, `10.13.1` on the uni-app and Taro application sides.
- MySQL and Redis; see `backend/configs/data.yaml` for default connections.
- Docker deployment requires a working Docker CLI and Docker daemon.
- Buf, protoc plugins, Wire and gorm-gen are only required when regenerating code and can be installed via `make -C backend init`.

Directly execute `make` or `make help` to view warehouse-level commands; use `make -C backend help` and `make -C frontend help` to view the complete targets of Backend and Frontend respectively.

## Local startup

Create the database first:

```sql
CREATE DATABASE kratos_admin CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
```

Install front-end dependencies:

```bash
make -C frontend init
```

If the dependency directory needs to be completely rebuilt:

```bash
make -C frontend reinstall
```

starts the backend:

```bash
make -C backend run
```

`run` will first refresh the interfaces, documents and Wire products required for startup; you can use `make -C backend run-only` to start directly when confirming that the generated products have not changed. For the complete target, execution sequence and parameters, see [Backend Common Process](backend/README.md#常用流程).

Start the management background, uni-app or Taro H5 (each command should be run in a separate terminal):

```bash
make -C frontend run-admin
cd frontend/uni-app && pnpm dev:h5
cd ../taro-app && pnpm dev:h5
```

| Services | Default Address |
| --- | --- |
| Backend HTTP | `http://localhost:7001` |
| Backend gRPC | `localhost:6001` |
| Management backend | `http://localhost:8848` |
| uni-app H5 | `http://localhost:5004` |
| Taro H5 | `http://localhost:5002` |

uni-app and Taro H5 use `5004` and `5002` respectively by default and can be started at the same time. When a LAN device accesses uni-app, replace `localhost` with the development machine LAN IP.

The default migration provides development accounts `super / 112233` and `admin / 112233`. Default passwords, JWT keys, database and Redis credentials must be modified before deployment.

## Generate and check

```bash
make -C backend gen
make check
make -C frontend build-all
```

`make check` Performs checks in the order of Backend, management module boundary, management backend, uni-app, and Taro. `build-all` builds the H5 host of the management background and the two application sides; generates all npm release packages using `make -C frontend package`, and the WeChat applet still executes `pnpm build:mp-weixin` of each workspace separately.

The backend builds `linux/amd64` binary by default through `make -C backend build`, and generates a release compressed package containing `bin/server` and `configs` through `make -C backend package`; the target platform can be used `GOOS`, `GOARCH` override.

The Docker image is built with the existing Backend command:

```bash
make -C backend docker-build IMAGE=kratos-admin TAG=latest
make -C backend docker-run IMAGE=kratos-admin TAG=latest
make -C backend docker-stop IMAGE=kratos-admin TAG=latest
```

The build command checks Docker before building the admin backend, uni-app H5, Taro H5 and Linux backend programs. Run the command to publish the host's `7001/6001` port, map `backend/data` to `/app/data`, and map to `/app/configs` after the first initialization of `backend/runtime/configs`, which can be modified by the host. The three-terminal static site is released with the image and merged into `/app/data` at startup. Existing uploaded files will not be cleared. For complete build parameters and running examples, see [Backend Building and Packaging](backend/README.md#构建与打包).

`I18N_LOCALES` Unified control of target languages ​​for project documentation and OpenAPI using a comma-separated list of BCP 47 language codes (default `en-US,zh-TW,ja-JP`). `make i18n-docs` collects README and docs Markdown from `scripts/project_docs.py` in the warehouse according to the three path ranges, and then generates `docs.json` and `docs.<locale>.json`; the corresponding `README.en-US.md`, `guide.ja-JP.md` Use it directly when the language source file exists, otherwise machine translation will be performed. The language directory only localizes the document body and display file name, `README.md` display name, directory name and stable path remain unchanged. To use an external implementation, override the script path via `PROJECT_DOCS_SCRIPT`. `make i18n-openapi` Generates OpenAPI multilingual YAML. Use `I18N_OFFLINE=1 make i18n` for offline generation.

`backend/api/gen`, `backend/internal/data/gen`, `backend/internal/docs/assets/docs*.json`, `backend/internal/docs/docs.go`, `src/rpc`, OpenAPI and `wire_gen.go` of each front-end package They are all generated products and cannot be modified manually. The Buf configuration of all front-end RPC is uniformly located in `backend/api`, the management side is generated through `make -C backend ts-admin`, and the application side is generated through `make -C backend ts-uni-app` and `make -C backend ts-taro-app` respectively; execute `make -C backend ts` when three terminals need to be generated at one time.

`make -C backend gen` will simultaneously generate the public entry internal Wire product of `backend/internal/module` and the independent startup Wire product of `backend/internal/cmd/server`; to refresh the former separately, use `make -C backend public-wire`, and to refresh the custom combination root separately, you can `WIRE_DIR` specifies the directory containing `wire.go`.

The external Go project merges the named modules, resources, scheduled tasks, SSE streams and queue consumer contributions of `github.com/liujitcn/kratos-admin/backend` with its own contributions, and then hands it over to `github.com/liujitcn/kratos-core` to create protocol services and application life cycles; external generated code will not reference `backend/internal`.

`make i18n-openapi` will generate `openapi.en-US.yaml`, `openapi.zh-TW.yaml` and `openapi.ja-JP.yaml` synchronously after generating `openapi.yaml`. Default resources come from the back-end error directory and the management-side Core language pack; external resources can be passed in through `OPENAPI_I18N_CONTENT="语言=路径"`. Missing copy is automatically translated by default: English and Japanese use Google V1, Traditional Chinese uses OpenCC; set `I18N_AUTO_LOCALIZE=0` to turn off automatic translation. Use `I18N_OFFLINE=1 make i18n-openapi` in a non-network environment.

## Internationalization

The language package defines the set of languages ​​that the system can render. The `base_language` table is only responsible for the runtime enablement status, name, sorting and main language configuration. The admin language preference is saved as `kratos-admin:locale`, uni-app and Taro are saved as `kratos-app:locale`; all HTTP, refresh token, fetch, SSE, uni.request and Taro.request requests will send the canonical `Accept-Language`. The fixed copy is maintained by the core/System JSON language package of each workspace. The dynamic menu and dictionary are parsed by the back-end translation table according to the requested language. If the current language translation is missing, it will fall back to the main language.

Adding new languages ​​does not require modification of Go, TypeScript or module registration code: add JSON with the same name in the back-end error directory and the six front-end language package directories of the three workspaces, and add data with the same name in the code generation `catalog.json`, and then execute `make i18n-sync`. The script validates language collections, language keys, and placeholders, and generates six front-end registration files, Element Plus, and Day.js mappings. The language name, sorting, enabled status, and primary language are provided by the `base_language` database record; `common.language.*` is the initial name used for offline display at compile time and for generating language migrations. The complete file list and migration process for the new languages ​​can be found in the [Internationalization Language Extension Guide](docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md). When you need to add a language to a new deployment database, execute `make i18n-sync I18N_MIGRATION_VERSION=vX.Y.Z` again and submit the versioned `base_language` migration generated by the script; the enabled status of the existing database will not be overwritten by the migration.

The main language of the dynamic resource is configured by `base_language.is_primary`. When creating or updating menus, dictionaries, dictionary items and system configurations, the backend converts the input text into the main language according to the request `Accept-Language` and writes it into the main table; when the requested language is not the main language, the original text is written into the corresponding translation table, and other enabled non-main languages ​​are only saved in the translation table. The system configuration name, menu title, dictionary name and dictionary item label support clicking on the name on the management side to open a translation pop-up window, and text/rich text configuration values ​​support runtime translation fallback.

Common commands for internationalization:

```bash
make i18n-check
make i18n-sync
make i18n-docs
make i18n-openapi
make i18n
```

The new language is directly written into the current `v0.0.1` migration:

```bash
I18N_LOCALE=ja-JP make i18n-locale
I18N_LOCALE=de-DE I18N_OFFLINE=1 make i18n-locale
```

Online mode uses Google V1, offline mode uses the built-in glossary and OpenCC. JSON and SQL should be audited after generation; the language enablement status of existing databases will not be overwritten. The runtime translation form can still perform real-time translation of dynamic resources, and existing non-empty translations will not be overwritten.

## Release

Unified release update and release 10 npm packages:

- `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-system`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-cli`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-core`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-ui`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-system`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli`

```bash
make tag VERSION=0.0.18
```

`make tag` will first execute `make i18n-docs` to refresh the embedded project document, and then the release script will submit the document and version update together. The script requires that the current branch is the remote default branch and synchronized with `origin`, performs back-end testing and front-end packaging, and then pushes `vX.Y.Z`, `backend/vX.Y.Z`, `npm/vX.Y.Z`. `npm/vX.Y.Z` triggers `.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` and publishes the above 10 packages through npm Trusted Publishing; the three default hosts are all private packages and do not participate in publishing. This machine requires available `git`, `gh` and GitHub login status.

only does local npm publishing:

```bash
pnpm login
make -C frontend publish
```

The publishing script will skip packages of the same version that already exist in the registry and support retrying after failure. Private registries can be overridden via `NPM_REGISTRY`, `NPM_ACCESS` and `NPM_TAG`.

## Documentation

| Topics | Documentation |
| --- | --- |
| Overall architecture | [docs/Overall system design.md](docs/系统总体设计.md) |
| New capability access | [docs/Service Access Guide.md](docs/服务接入指南.md) |
| Database migration | [docs/Database and initialization data design.md](docs/数据库与初始化数据设计.md) |
| Parameter verification | [docs/Interface parameter verification design.md](docs/接口参数校验设计.md) |
| Login and Password | [docs/Login and Password Encryption Process.md](docs/登录与密码加密流程.md) |
| AI Assistant | [docs/AI Assistant Design.md](docs/AI助手设计.md) |
| Management component | [docs/front-end component list.md](docs/前端组件清单.md) |
| International design | [docs/Final internationalization plan.md](docs/国际化最终方案.md) |
| New language | [docs/International Language Extension Guide.md](docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md) |

# backend

`backend` retains the API contract, Go generated interface, Service implementation, Biz business layer, as well as task scheduling, HTTP/gRPC/MCP/AI registration and necessary data access closures; the process entry is at `internal/cmd/server`. The root package is provided by `ProviderSet`, `NewModuleResources`, `NewModules`, `NewTasks`, `NewStreams` and `NewQueueConsumers` Hosting a common boundary for reuse, `internal/module` only hosts internal implementations. AI Runtime is implemented in `internal/biz`, and the external reuse entry is `pkg/agent`.

## Table of Contents

```text
backend
├── internal/cmd/server             # Admin 独立启动入口与 Wire 组合根
├── api
│   ├── proto                         # Proto 契约
│   └── gen/go                        # Buf 生成的 Go 接口、HTTP、gRPC 和工具代码
├── internal/biz                      # 业务 Case、DTO、代码生成和辅助领域代码
├── bootstrap.go                      # 对外 ProviderSet 和模块/任务/SSE/队列/资源入口
├── internal/module                   # Admin 到 kratos-core 的内部模块适配和资源实现
│   ├── module.go                     # Core Module 协议注册
│   ├── resources.go                  # module.Module 静态资源
│   ├── init.go                        # Admin 模块 ProviderSet
│   └── wire.go / wire_gen.go          # 公共入口使用的内部依赖装配
├── pkg/agent                         # 对外复用的 AI Runtime、模型和工具 API
├── internal/task                     # 异步任务与定时任务执行器
├── internal/server                   # 服务中间件和 API 模块注册适配
├── internal/task                     # 异步业务任务
├── internal/data/gen                 # GORM 生成的模型、查询和仓储
├── internal/service                  # Proto Service 实现
├── internal/const                    # 业务常量
├── internal/i18n/assets              # 业务语言资源
└── migration                         # 代码生成业务使用的迁移资源
```

## Common processes

After entering the `backend` directory, first use the help to view all targets, parameter default values ​​and override examples:

```bash
make help
```

First development installation of Buf, protoc, Wire, gorm-gen, goimports and inspection tools:

```bash
make init
```

Daily startup use:

```bash
make run
```

`make run` will refresh the necessary products in the order of "Project Document -> protobuf Go -> OpenAPI -> Independent Entry Wire -> Start Service". When it is confirmed that there is no change in the generated product, you can skip the generation and start directly:

```bash
make run-only
```

The default configuration directory is `./configs`, you can overwrite the configuration directory or add startup parameters:

```bash
make run-only CONF=/path/to/configs
make run-only RUN_ARGS='--help'
```

independent entrance injection `kratoscore.ProviderSet` and internal module ProviderSet; Core is responsible for unified creation and management of HTTP, gRPC, MCP, SSE, queue and scheduled task runtime.

## Execute after modification

| Modify Scenario | Command | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proto Contract | `make api openapi ts` | Generates TypeScript RPCs for Go, OpenAPI, and three frontends. Use `ts-admin`, `ts-uni-app` or `ts-taro-app` instead when affecting only one frontend. |
| Database table structure | `make gorm-gen` | Update the development library first, and then generate it according to `GORM_GEN_CONFIG`, `GORM_GEN_DATABASE` and `GORM_TABLE`. |
| ProviderSet or construction parameter | `make public-wire wire` | Refresh the public entrance internal assembly and independent service entrance respectively. |
| README or docs | `make project-docs` | Collect Markdown and generate document directories in each language. |
| Language pack or internationalization resource | `make i18n` | Synchronize language packs, project documents and OpenAPI multi-language products in sequence. |
| Multiple types of generation sources change simultaneously | `make gen` | Execute GORM, interface, front-end, document, Wire and formatting in sequence; access to the development database is required. |

All generated products must be refreshed through the above command and cannot be modified manually.

## Check

Performs a full Backend check before committing:

```bash
make check
```

`make check` Running `make lint`, `make test`, and `make i18n-check` in that order does not automatically format the code. When formatting is required, execute first:

```bash
make fmt
```

can also run an item individually:

```bash
make lint
make test
make i18n-check
```

## Building and packaging

builds the executable files of `linux/amd64` and `CGO_ENABLED=0` by default:

```bash
make build
```

is `bin/server`. The release compressed package contains both the executable file and the `configs` directory:

```bash
make package
```

Default output is `dist/backend-linux-amd64.tar.gz`. Other platforms can override parameters:

```bash
make package GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64
make build GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 BINARY=bin/server-darwin-arm64
```

After decompressing the release package, it can be started through `./bin/server --conf ./configs`. The database, Redis, JWT and other deployment configurations in `configs` should be checked before packaging, and do not publish local credentials directly.

The built-in `docker-build` in the warehouse will first verify the Docker CLI and Docker daemon, and then build the management backend, uni-app H5, Taro H5, Linux backend program and final image in sequence:

```bash
make docker-build \
  IMAGE=kratos-admin \
  TAG=v1.0.0
```

generates the `linux/amd64` image by default. Specify both Go and Docker platforms when building an ARM64 image:

```bash
make docker-build GOARCH=arm64 DOCKER_PLATFORM=linux/arm64
```

image saves the three-terminal static site in a read-only seed directory, and merges it into `/app/data` when the container starts. Images, attachments and other runtime files uploaded by local OSS are also located in `/app/data`, so the entire directory should be bound to the host during deployment; the startup script only overwrites the site files provided by the image and does not clear the existing upload directory.

After the local build is completed, use `docker-run` to start the container:

```bash
make docker-run IMAGE=kratos-admin TAG=v1.0.0
```

This command uses a bridged network by default and publishes the host `7001`, `6001` ports. The first run will initialize `configs/*.yaml` to the host `runtime/configs`, change the local address of MySQL, Redis, Consul and other containers to actively connect to `host.docker.internal`, and then read-only map it to `/app/configs`; the OAuth browser callback address remains unchanged. Modify the YAML in `runtime/configs` on the host and then restart the container to take effect. There is no need to rebuild the image.

Host `data` maps to `/app/data`. Data, configuration, network and publishing ports can be overridden via `DOCKER_DATA_DIR`, `DOCKER_CONFIG_DIR`, `DOCKER_NETWORK`, `DOCKER_HTTP_PORT`, `DOCKER_GRPC_PORT`. Delete `runtime/configs` and execute `make docker-run` again to reinitialize the running configuration according to the current `configs`.

stops the local service but retains container and host data:

```bash
make docker-stop IMAGE=kratos-admin TAG=v1.0.0
```

will automatically clean up the stopped container with the same name and recreate it.

image itself will not contain `configs/*_local.yaml`, historical upload files, code generation recovery files, or run logs. `docker-run` After mounting the host configuration directory, the local configuration file is only visible to the container during runtime.

## Common parameters

| Parameters | Default value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONF` | `./configs` | Service running configuration directory. |
| `RUN_ARGS` | Empty | Parameters appended to the service command. |
| `CGO_ENABLED` | `0` | Whether to enable CGO when building Go. |
| `GOOS` / `GOARCH` | `linux` / `amd64` | Build the target platform. |
| `BINARY` | `bin/server` | Executable file output path. |
| `ARCHIVE` | `dist/backend-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` | Publish the compressed package output path. |
| `DOCKER` | `docker` | Docker command path or name. |
| `DOCKERFILE` | `Dockerfile` | Dockerfile path. |
| `DOCKER_PLATFORM` | `linux/<GOARCH>` | Mirror target platform. |
| `IMAGE` / `TAG` | `backend` / `latest` | Docker image name and label. |
| `CONTAINER_NAME` | `kratos-admin` | The name of the locally running container. |
| `DOCKER_NETWORK` | `bridge` | Container network. |
| `DOCKER_HTTP_PORT` | `7001` | Maps to the host HTTP port of container `7001`. |
| `DOCKER_GRPC_PORT` | `6001` | The host gRPC port mapped to container `6001`. |
| `DOCKER_DATA_DIR` | `backend/data` | Host directory mapped to `/app/data`. |
| `DOCKER_CONFIG_SOURCE_DIR` | `backend/configs` | The source directory for initializing the Docker run configuration for the first time. |
| `DOCKER_CONFIG_DIR` | `backend/runtime/configs` | Read-only host runtime configuration directory mapped to `/app/configs`. |
| `DOCKER_RUN_ARGS` | Null | Additional parameters passed to `docker run`. |
| `PUBLIC_WIRE_DIR` | `internal/module` | The directory where the internal `wire.go` is used by the public entry. |
| `WIRE_DIR` | `internal/cmd/server` | The directory where the independent entry `wire.go` is located. |
| `GORM_GEN_CONFIG` | `configs/data_local.yaml` | The data source configuration used by GORM generation. |
| `GORM_GEN_DATABASE` | Empty | Optional database name, the configuration file is read by default. |
| `GORM_TABLE` | List of built-in tables | Comma-separated list of GORM generated tables. |
| `I18N_LOCALES` | `en-US,zh-TW,ja-JP` | Documentation and target language for OpenAPI. |
| `I18N_OFFLINE` | `0` | Disable online translation when set to `1`. |
| `PROJECT_DOCS_SCRIPT` | `../scripts/project_docs.py` | Project document collection and localization scripts. |

## External host reuse

When an external Go project reuses Backend, add `kratoscore.ProviderSet`, `backend.ProviderSet` and the host's merged ProviderSet to its own Wire combination root:

```go
func NewApp(ctx *bootstrap.Context) (*kratos.App, func(), error) {
	panic(wire.Build(
		kratoscore.ProviderSet,
		backend.ProviderSet,
		mergeProviderSet,
	))
}
```

The root package outputs named contributions via `AdminResources`, `AdminModules`, `AdminTasks`, `AdminStreams`, and `AdminConsumers`, the merged ProviderSet of the host Explicitly append them with contributions from other business modules as the Core final collection. The public constructor only uses Core public types, and the externally generated `wire_gen.go` will not depend on `backend/internal`.

`backend.NewModules` initializes the host process-level running log collector; after the external project is connected to Backend in the above way, the logs written by itself and other registered modules to stdout/stderr will also enter the running log real-time console, and the historical log files will be read according to the host's log configuration.

Use `pkg/agent.NewRuntime` when external modules are connected to AI to create runtime and register Eino through `RuntimeConfig.AdminTools/AppTools` or `Runtime.RegisterTool`; simple structured tools are preferred to use `pkg/agent.InferTool` Automatically generate parameter schema. Fixed processes such as comment moderation and content extraction can combine `NewChatClient`, `NewStructuredRunner`, `SchemaFor` and multimodal Part constructors without referencing the `internal` package. Implement `ToolAccessChecker` when permission control is required. If not connected to the permission system, keep `Checker` as `nil`.

# AI assistant

AI assistant is a conversational capability shared by the management side, uni-app and Taro application side. The three portals use the same set of `base.v1` interfaces and data tables, but filter the available tools and shortcut portals by terminal.

## Implemented capabilities

- Session creation, listing, renaming, deleting and persisting branches.
- Message list, text and attachment sending, editing last message, deletion, failed retry and regeneration.
- `delta`, `finish`, `error` Direct streaming responses to three types of SSE events.
- Markdown, model source, Token, first Token time consumption, total time consumption and tool call record.
- Filters generated Agent Tools by terminal, interface switch, and user permissions.
- Fixed process quick entry and structured actions; old message actions will be judged as expired by the server.
- Responses server tool record; returns an explicit unavailable error when the current model is not enabled.

## Contract and data

| Capabilities | Proto | HTTP Prefix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quick entry | `backend/api/proto/base/v1/ai_tool.proto` | `/api/v1/base/ai/shortcut` |
| Session | `ai_session.proto` | `/api/v1/base/ai/session` |
| Messages | `ai_message.proto` | `/api/v1/base/ai/session/{session_id}/message` |

data is persisted to `ai_session` and `ai_message`. A round of messages saves input, output, attachments, tools, tokens, time consumption, status and optional structured process content. The action must carry `source_message_id`, `action_id` and `flow_version` of the current latest success message.

The HTTP handler that sends the message returns `text/event-stream` directly, without using the generic `/events/{stream}` subscription. At the end of the stream the `finish` event returns the final message and updated session.

## Backend link

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  API["AiMessageService"] --> Case["AiMessageCase"]
  Case --> Runtime["biz/base/ai.Runtime"]
  Runtime --> ADK["internal/agent/adk"]
  ADK --> Model["Eino Agentic Model"]
  ADK --> Tools["按终端和权限筛选的工具"]
  Case --> DB[("ai_session / ai_message")]
```

`internal/biz/base/ai` is responsible for business protocols, historical messages, attachments, terminal policies, fixed processes and result persistence; `internal/agent` isolates Eino's model, messages, ADK, Middleware, Callback, Tool, Structured and Workflow details.

Agent Tool comes from generated code, `agent_status` controls whether it can be used by AI; `mcp_status` independently controls whether it is exposed as MCP Tool. The two are not the same switch.

## Management end

The management terminal is located at `frontend/admin/packages/modules/system/src/views/ai/chat`:

| Documentation | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| `index.vue` | General orchestration of conversations, messages, sends and actions. |
| `components/SessionPanel.vue` | Session search, creation, switching, renaming and deletion. |
| `components/ChatPanel.vue` | Message area, empty state, shortcut entry and message operation. |
| `components/XSender.vue` | Text, attachments, and delivery status. |
| `components/AiMarkdown.vue` | Markdown and code content. |
| `stream.ts`, `message.ts` | SSE parsing and message status normalization. |

The System module also registers the AI ​​icon as a top tool. The Structured Process Block component is not a built-in fixed implementation; other business modules may provide `flowBlocks` extensions via `ADMIN_AI_EXTENSION`.

## Application side

uni-app is located at `frontend/uni-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai` and Taro is located at `frontend/taro-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai`. Both ends provide session drawers, welcome shortcuts, input and attachments, message flows, and multi-end SSE parsing. The pages belong to the `pagesMember` subpackage and use the same `base.v1` RPC and API encapsulation. H5 uses Fetch SSE; WeChat applets use the chunked request capabilities of their respective platforms.

## Configuration and verification

model configuration is located at `backend/configs/ai.yaml` and `ai_local.yaml`. The service can still be started when no model configuration is provided, but the AI ​​runtime is turned off.

executes back-end generation and testing after modifying the protocol or runtime; modifies the management side to execute `pnpm lint:oxlint`, `pnpm type:check`; modifies uni-app or Taro to execute `pnpm lint`, `pnpm tsc` of the corresponding workspace, involving the module protocol or runner Then execute `pnpm test`, `pnpm check:exports`. The front-end checks at least empty session, historical session, sending, failed, attachment and expired process action status.

- [Proto and HTTP Contract](../backend/docs/api.md): Protocol, path, generation and permissions synchronization.
- [Error Handling](../backend/docs/errors.md): Error classification, metadata, and hierarchical responsibilities.

## Document maintenance

- The document only describes the currently existing capabilities of the warehouse; planned capabilities must be clearly marked as "unimplemented" and cannot be written as the current status.
- Command, path, package name and interface are subject to code, Makefile, Proto and package `exports`.
- After modifying the README, `docs` or backend details, execute `make i18n-docs` to update the embedded project documentation.
- `I18N_LOCALES` uses a comma-separated list of BCP 47 language codes to control the target language of OpenAPI and project Markdown documents at the same time; `make i18n-docs` is collected from the warehouse `scripts/project_docs.py` first collects default and existing language Markdown, and then generates `docs.json` and `docs.<locale>.json` without the `locale` field. The language directory only localizes the document text and non-README display file names, and the directory name and stable path remain unchanged; external scripts can also be specified through `PROJECT_DOCS_SCRIPT`. `make i18n-openapi` Generates OpenAPI multilingual YAML. `I18N_OFFLINE=1` can be set if there is no network environment.
- The generated `backend/internal/docs/assets/docs*.json` and `backend/internal/docs/docs.go` can only be updated via `make i18n-docs`.

documents.content:
# Front-end component list

This article only records the components and their boundaries that exist in the current code and can be used directly. The management component implementation is located in `frontend/admin/packages/core/src/components`; the base components, UI packages and page private components of uni-app and Taro belong to their respective workspaces.

## Management-side public components

| Scenario | Component | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paged lists, searches, column settings, bulk operations | `ProTable` | Configure lists using `columns`, `headerActions`, and `requestApi`. |
| Add or edit pop-up window | `FormDialog` | Combining `ProDialog` and `ProForm`, the page is responsible for verification, submission and refresh. |
| Details, preview, or non-form popup | `ProDialog` | Content organized by default or named slots. |
| Configuration form | `ProForm` | Fields are described by `ProFormField[]` and support existing controls such as input, selection, dictionary, upload, and rich text. |
| Dictionary selection and display | `Dict`, `DictLabel` | Registered as a global component by the core startup process. |
| Image upload | `UploadImg` | Core's public upload component; multi-image and file upload are currently only for core internal use. |
| Tree filter | `TreeFilter` | Support static data or request loading, single selection and multi-selection. |
| Icon selection | `SelectIcon` | Select the Element Plus icon name. |
| Markdown read-only preview | `MarkdownPreview` | Encapsulation `md-editor-v3`, unified security cleaning, code highlighting, light and dark themes and compact code block style. |
| Rich text | `WangEditor` | Encapsulate wangEditor and reuse the file upload service. |
| Password strength | `PasswordStrength` | Login, user and personal center password form usage. |

`CronExpression`, `ECharts`, `Grid`, `ImportExcel`, `SelectFilter`, `SwitchDark` and other components do exist but have not been passed through npm `exports` is open and should only be used within core. Whether it can be referenced across packages is subject to `frontend/admin/packages/core/package.json#exports`, and the source code directory cannot be regarded as a public interface.

## Public import entry

The business module uses the core package to expose the entry and does not reference `packages/core/src`:

```ts
import ProTable from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/ProTable";
import FormDialog from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/Dialog/FormDialog.vue";
import MarkdownPreview from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/MarkdownPreview/index.vue";
import type {
  ColumnProps,
  HeaderActionProps,
  ProTableInstance
} from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/ProTable/interface";
import type {
  ProFormField,
  ProFormInstance
} from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/ProForm/interface";
```

The currently exposed Vue component entries are as follows:

| Components | npm entry |
| --- | --- |
| `FormDialog` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/Dialog/FormDialog.vue` |
| `ProDialog` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/Dialog/ProDialog.vue` |
| `DictLabel` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/Dict/DictLabel.vue` |
| `MarkdownPreview` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/MarkdownPreview/index.vue` |
| `PasswordStrength` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/PasswordStrength/index.vue` |
| `ProForm` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/ProForm/index.vue` |
| `ProTable` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/ProTable` |
| `SelectIcon` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/SelectIcon/index.vue` |
| `TreeFilter` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/TreeFilter/index.vue` |
| `UploadImg` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/Upload/Img.vue` |
| `WangEditor` | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/components/WangEditor/index.vue` |

`bootstrapAdminApp` also globally registers the Element Plus icon as well as `Dict`, `DictLabel`, `SvgIcon`. Global registration facilitates direct use of templates and does not mean that the corresponding source code path has become a public entrance to npm.

## Lists and forms

### ProTable

`ProTable` is defined in `packages/core/src/components/ProTable/interface/index.ts`. Common configurations include:

- `columns`: columns, search terms, dictionaries, status and row operations.
- `requestApi`: paging request, return `{ data: { list, total } }`.
- `headerActions`: Header operations such as new addition and batch deletion.
- `cellType`: Existing `image`, `status`, `actions`, `money` cells.
- `dictCode`: Use system dictionary display or search.

page request uses core's table tool to convert paging parameters:

```ts
import { buildPageRequest } from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/table";

async function requestTable(params: Record<string, unknown>) {
  const response = await service.PageResource(buildPageRequest(params));
  return {
    data: {
      list: response.resources ?? [],
      total: response.total
    }
  };
}
```

table instance provides the ability to re-request, search, reset, clear selection, and read the current selection and paging status. The specific type is subject to `ProTableInstance`.

### ProForm and FormDialog

`ProFormField` currently supports input boxes, numbers, segmented selections, check boxes, switches, drop-downs, radio selections, multi-selections, dictionaries, tree selections, dates, Cron, shuttle boxes, image and file uploads, rich text, dynamic lists, key-value lists and custom slots.

A typical pop-up window only needs to expose components and field types:

```vue
<FormDialog
  ref="dialogRef"
  v-model="dialogVisible"
  :model="formModel"
  :fields="formFields"
  :rules="rules"
  @confirm="handleSubmit"
  @closed="resetForm"
/>
```

`FormDialog` is only responsible for interaction and verification entry, and does not automatically call the business interface. The page executes `validate()` in the confirmation event, submits the service, closes the pop-up window and refreshes the form. After closing, the model and verification status are explicitly reset.

## Markdown Preview

`MarkdownPreview` is used for read-only content such as project documentation, database migration instructions, and AI replies. The component uniformly injects local Highlight.js in the core, uses DOMPurify to clean rendering results, generates anchor points compatible with Chinese and repeated titles, and turns off Mermaid, KaTeX, ECharts, image enlargement, code folding and code line numbers.

```vue
<MarkdownPreview
  :model-value="content"
  :is-dark="globalStore.isDark"
  max-code-height="360px"
/>
```

`modelValue` is the original Markdown text, `isDark` follows the host theme, and `maxCodeHeight` only limits the maximum height of long code blocks. Single-line and double-line code blocks are always rendered at the actual content height. Business modules must no longer rely directly on the underlying `md-editor-v3` or maintain another set of Markdown themes.

## Internal components

The following components are existing implementations but are not listed in the public npm entry:

| Table of Contents | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| `components/Card` | Data overview card. |
| `components/CronExpression` | Six-section Cron editor. |
| `components/ECharts` | Bar, Line, Pie and other chart containers. |
| `components/ErrorMessage` | 403, 404, 500 and other error status display. |
| `components/Grid`, `SearchForm` | Responsive layout for the ProTable search area. |
| `components/ImportExcel` | Excel file import pop-up window. |
| `components/Loading` | Page and full screen loading status. |
| `components/SelectFilter` | Multiple sets of filter conditions. |
| `components/SwitchDark` | Switch between light and dark themes. |
| `components/Upload` | Upload single image, multiple images, single file, and multiple files. |

When the business module requires one of the capabilities, first confirm whether there is a public entrance. If there is indeed a need for cross-module reuse, add a clear single-component entry in `package.json#exports` of the core, and synchronize construction and type checking; do not add `components/*` wildcard export.

## Layout and page components

Four management-side layouts are located in `frontend/admin/packages/core/src/layouts`: `LayoutVertical`, `LayoutClassic`, `LayoutTransverse`, `LayoutColumns`. They are selected by core routing and global settings and are not used as business page components.

The page private components of the System module are located in `frontend/admin/packages/modules/system/src/views/**/components`, such as the user page department tree, personal center form and code generation preview components. `src/components/Ai.vue` is the AI ​​entry System registered to the top toolbar. None of these components currently have npm public exports.

## Application component

uni-app core provides two base components `BootstrapStatus` and `KratosTabBar`. The public entrance is subject to `@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core/components/*.vue`; Taro core provides the corresponding `BootstrapStatus`, `KratosPageFrame` and `KratosTabBar`, and exposed through `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-core/components/*`. Taro's `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-ui` is also responsible for NutUI theme and icon entry, but does not host business pages.

The following components are private components of the AI ​​page in the two application-side system modules:

| Component | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `frontend/uni-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai/components/Composer.vue` | uni-app message input, attachment and send operations. |
| `frontend/uni-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai/components/SessionDrawer.vue` | uni-app session list and switching. |
| `frontend/uni-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai/components/WelcomePanel.vue` | uni-app AI page welcome area and quick entry. |
| `frontend/taro-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai/components/Composer.tsx` | Taro message entry, attachment and send operations. |
| `frontend/taro-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai/components/SessionDrawer.tsx` | Taro session list and switching. |
| `frontend/taro-app/packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai/components/WelcomePanel.tsx` | Taro AI page welcome area and quick entry. |

They only serve their respective `pagesMember/ai` pages and are not part of the public component interface of the application base. After at least two pages are truly reused without business semantics, consider upgrading them to the public component directory of the corresponding workspace.

## Maintenance basis

- Management side public export: `frontend/admin/packages/core/package.json#exports`
- Management component source code: `frontend/admin/packages/core/src/components`
- System page and private components: `frontend/admin/packages/modules/system/src`
- uni-app base component: `frontend/uni-app/packages/core/src/components`
- Taro base assembly: `frontend/taro-app/packages/core/src/components`
- Taro UI theme and icon: `frontend/taro-app/packages/ui/src`
- Application page private component: `packages/modules/system/src/views/pagesMember/ai/components` of two workspaces

Component properties and instance methods are subject to the Vue/TypeScript type definitions in the same directory; this article does not copy the complete props to avoid retaining the invalidity of the document after adjustment.

documents.content:
# International design

This article describes the internationalization boundaries, runtime behavior, and data responsibilities currently implemented by the warehouse. The specific operation of adding a new language is subject to the [International Language Expansion Guide] (国际化语言扩展指南.md).

## Current conclusion

| Content | Current Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Fixed language pack | `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `en-US`, `ja-JP` |
| Compile-time default language | `zh-CN` |
| Dynamic resource main language | Determined by `base_language.is_primary` |
| Fixed copywriting | core/System JSON language pack for three front-end workspaces |
| Backend Error | Structured JSON directory for `backend/internal/i18n/assets` |
| Runtime language options | `base_language` Enabled languages returned by interface |
| Dynamic Resources | Menus, dictionaries, dictionary entries, and system configuration name/value translation tables |
| Machine Translation | Empty translations can be generated and saved on demand; existing non-empty translations will not be overwritten |

Internationalization is not about putting all language names or translation constants into the database. The database is responsible for deployment and configuration, and the language package is responsible for the whitelist and fixed copy during compilation; new languages ​​must update both layers at the same time.

## Runtime link

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Files["语言包 JSON"] --> Sync["scripts/sync_locales.py"]
  Sync --> UI["固定 UI 与错误目录"]
  DB["base_language"] --> Options["运行时语言选项"]
  Request["Accept-Language"] --> Locale["locale 规范化"]
  Locale --> UI
  Locale --> Dynamic["动态菜单/字典/配置解析"]
  Dynamic --> Tables[("翻译表")]
```

### Compile-time language collection

`scripts/sync_locales.py` Scans the following seven language pack directories and additionally verifies the code generator's `catalog.json`:

```text
backend/internal/i18n/assets
frontend/admin/packages/core/src/locales
frontend/admin/packages/modules/system/src/locales
frontend/uni-app/packages/core/src/locales
frontend/uni-app/packages/modules/system/src/locales
frontend/taro-app/packages/core/src/locales
frontend/taro-app/packages/modules/system/src/locales
backend/internal/biz/system/admin/codegen/locales/catalog.json
```

The file set, fixed keys and placeholders of the seven language pack directories must be consistent; `catalog.json` must also contain the same language code and fixed fields. The script generates six front-end `generated.ts` and verifies the locale mapping of Day.js and Element Plus on the management side. Core's `resource/i18n` receives host language resources. Core is responsible for directory loading and error localization internally, and does not embed project entries. The generated files cannot be modified manually.

### Runtime language configuration

`base_language` Save:

- `language_code`: canonical BCP 47 language code;
- `language_name`, `native_name`: Management terminal and login page display name;
- `status`, `sort`: whether optional and display order;
- `is_primary`: Primary language for dynamic menus, dictionaries and system configuration.

When the front end is started, it first uses the compile-time package to establish a fallback language list, and then requests the public language interface; when the database interface succeeds, it is based on the enabled language and sorting, and when it fails, it falls back to the compile-time language list. The deployment configuration should only enable languages ​​that have been published with the package, the database records themselves will not generate missing language packages.

### Requests and rollbacks

Management-side Axios, refresh token, fetch, SSE and Swagger requests, as well as uni-app/Taro requests, uploads and SSE, uniformly send standardized `Accept-Language`. The backend matches the area according to the whitelist, and falls back to `zh-CN` for unknown values.

The rollback sequence is as follows:

```text
固定 UI：当前语言 -> zh-CN -> 安全默认文案
菜单/字典/配置：当前语言非空翻译 -> 主表主语言字段 -> 稳定 code/path
错误：当前语言 message_key -> zh-CN message_key -> 原始安全消息 -> INTERNAL_ERROR
```

does not display raw keys, unsaved machine translation results, database errors, SQL or third-party provider responses at runtime.

## Fixed copywriting and error directory

Each front-end module maintains its own JSON language package, and the language set, key, namespace and placeholder are verified when the module is registered. Core maintains general capabilities, System maintains system management, personal center and AI copywriting; modules must not directly modify the language package of another module.

The backend error directory is loaded by `go-i18n`. Proto `buf.validate`'s `id/message` and explicit `WithMessageKey` in Go must be defined in `zh-CN.json`, other languages ​​keep the same keys and placeholders. The check command is:

```bash
make i18n-check
```

keeps the existing `code/reason` externally, only adds stable `message_key/message_args` in the metadata, and renders `message` according to the request language by the response boundary.

## Front-end and back-end Key naming convention

The front-end and back-end use the same set of layered ideas, but retain the naming sources of their respective code ecosystems: the front-end fixed copy generates business paths from component names, and back-end errors generate business paths from Proto package and Service. Key is a stable technical identifier that does not contain Chinese characters and is not named based on translation results.

### Front-end fixed copywriting

Front-end fixed copy uses the following format:

```text
<模块>.<组件业务路径>.<文案类型>.<名称>
```

The component business path comes from `defineOptions.name`, split the PascalCase name into a lowercase dot path:

```text
BaseDict      -> base.dict
BaseDictItem  -> base.dict.item
CodeGenTable  -> code.gen.table
BaseTenant    -> base.tenant
```

Example:

```text
system.base.dict.title.create
system.base.dict.field.created_at
system.base.dict.dialog.confirm_status
system.base.dict.message.create_success
system.code.gen.table.field.page_type
```

Copy types use fixed collections: `title`, `field`, `section`, `action`, `placeholder`, `validation`, __KRA TOS_TOKEN_0006__, `message`, `error`, `status`, `value`, `tooltip`, `empty`. Names and fields use `snake_case` uniformly, such as `confirm_status`, `created_at`, `create_success`.

Use `common.*` for copywriting that is truly cross-business reusable, without adding business paths repeatedly:

```text
common.action.create
common.field.created_at
common.validation.required_input
```

The logical key of the front-end language package uses the above dotted path. The current runtime and verification code are still read according to the flat key; if the JSON is changed to a nested object, the synchronization script, module registration and generated product must be modified simultaneously, and the JSON shape cannot be changed manually.

### Backend error message

The backend `message_key` uses the following format:

```text
<package 去掉版本>.<Service 业务路径>.<操作或对象>.<字段>.<规则>
```

Proto package removes the version number, Service removes `Service` and then press PascalCase to split it into a lowercase dotted path:

```text
system.admin.v1 + BaseDictService -> system.admin.base.dict
system.admin.v1 + CodeGenTableService -> system.admin.code.gen.table
base.v1 + LoginService -> base.login
```

Example:

```text
system.admin.base.dict.entity.name.required
system.admin.base.dict.create.name.required
system.admin.base.dict.update.id.required
system.admin.code.gen.table.field.page_type.required
```

`entity` represents the verification of the entity itself, and other values ​​represent specific operations. Field names and rule names use Proto-style `snake_case`. Rule names should remain stable and given priority `required`, `max_length`, `min_length`, `format`, __KRATOS_T OKEN_0006__, `positive`, `non_negative`, `unique`, `supported` and other fixed vocabulary.

General error is not bound to a specific Service:

```text
common.error.invalid_argument
common.error.permission_denied
```

version number `v1` does not enter the key; `message_key` will be returned with the error response and is an external stable contract. The rename must be synchronized with Proto, Go, all language directories and the caller.

### Correspondence between front and back ends

The front and back ends are not required to use exactly the same key, but the business paths should be able to correspond to each other:

```text
前端：system.base.dict.dialog.confirm_status
后端：system.admin.base.dict.create.name.required
```

Dynamic menu, dictionary, configuration and other database translations use the target type and number of `base_i18n`, and do not reuse the fixed copy key.

## Dynamic resource translation

Dynamic resources share a translation table `base_i18n`, and the target resources are distinguished by `target_type`:

| `target_type` | Main table | Translatable fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1` | `base_config` | Text and rich text configuration values |
| `2` | `base_config` | System configuration name |
| `3` | `base_dict` | Dictionary name |
| `4` | `base_dict_item` | Dictionary item tag |
| `5` | `base_menu` | Menu title |

`base_dict.code` and `base_dict_item.value` are stable business identifiers and do not enter the translation table; the dictionary name and dictionary item label correspond to `3` and `4` respectively, and the system configuration name and value correspond respectively. `2` and `1`.

When creating or updating dynamic resources, the main language text is written to the main table; manually entered non-main language text is written directly to `base_i18n`. Uninputted languages ​​are supplemented by translation tasks, and existing non-empty translations will not be overwritten; the main language is not repeatedly saved in the translation table, and falls back to the main table if missing.

Fixed translations of built-in menus, dictionaries, dictionary entries and system configurations are located in the same version `i18n.<locale>.up.sql`. Migration uses idempotent `INSERT IGNORE`, which will not overwrite already maintained data; the executed version cannot be repaired by rewriting the file, and a new version must be added for migration.

## Machine translation

The machine translation of the service runtime is through `kratos-kit/translator` Press `backend/configs/translator.yaml` to select the Provider. The entry includes:

- Management side `BaseI18nService.DraftBaseI18n`: Generate and save a single translation for a saved menu, dictionary, dictionary item or configuration.
- After the menu, dictionary, dictionary item and configuration are successfully created or updated: the resource message is first delivered to the asynchronous translation queue; when the queue consumption fails, the scheduled task scans the pending translations.
- When the management-side editor submits empty text, or if a vacant translation is found when hovering the list name, it will be filled in immediately through the same interface; the non-empty translations filled in manually remain unchanged.

Batch language packs and migration translations are generated by calling independent scripts from `make i18n-locale I18N_LOCALE=<locale>` and are not part of the normal service request link.

The translation interface is turned off by default and can be turned on through `translator.enabled=true`, `I18N_DRAFT_ENABLED=true` or application metadata. The server reads the controlled source text, with the target language limited to the enabled language, calling it serially and using the HTTP timeout configured with `translator.timeout` (default 8 seconds); existing non-null translations will not be overwritten. System configuration names, text, and rich text type values ​​will enter machine translation, and images and Boolean values ​​will not be sent out.

Provider is only used for translation and cannot be used for login, error responses, plain CRUD or arbitrary text translation agents. When the Provider is unavailable, fixed language packs, existing translations, and primary language fallbacks must still work properly.

## Code generation

code generator uses the fixed template of `backend/internal/biz/system/admin/codegen/locales/catalog.json` and reads the business name and field name from the table level and field level `i18n_config`. The generation page will write the stable keys of all compilation-time languages; when the non-main language lacks necessary configurations, the missing items should be completed and displayed in the preview before official generation.

Generators must not write new Chinese UI copy directly into Vue, Proto or menu SQL. The generated results belong to the key range of the current code generation object and cannot cover other modules or manually maintained translations.

## Database migration

New languages ​​or new translations use a higher version directory:

```text
backend/migration/assets/vX.Y.Z/mysql/
├── language.up.sql
├── language.description.md
├── i18n.<locale>.up.sql
└── i18n.<locale>.description.md
```

`make i18n-sync I18N_MIGRATION_VERSION=vX.Y.Z` generates `base_language` initialization record; `make i18n-locale I18N_LOCALE=<locale>` writes the dynamic translation SQL into the current `v0.0.1` by default. If a new version directory is required, pass in `I18N_MIGRATION_VERSION=vX.Y.Z`. After generation, SQL and language packages should be checked before submitting the same version of the description file; language packages that have been completed manually should not be overwritten with batch scripts.

`base_language` are deployment configurations and should not be forcibly overridden by re-executing the language pack sync script. Executed migration files cannot be modified in the production environment.

## Verification Checklist

After adding or modifying a language, check at least:

1. `make i18n-check` and `make i18n-sync` pass.
2. The key and placeholder verification of the management end, uni-app, and Taro passed.
3. When the language interface fails, the three terminals can still use the compile-time fallback list.
4. Language selection can be restored before logging in, after logging in, refreshing and reopening the app.
5. Menus, dictionaries and configurations can all fall back correctly when there are non-empty translations, missing translations and primary language switching.
6. The reason for verification, authentication, permission and resource errors remains unchanged, only the message is localized.
7. The type check and lint of `go test ./...` and the affected workspace pass.

See the [Internationalization Language Extension Guide] (国际化语言扩展指南.md) for step-by-step commands, file lists, and troubleshooting for new languages.

documents.content:
# Internationalization Language Extension Guide

This article is the implementation manual for the new language. The current fixed language set is `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `en-US`, `ja-JP`. When adding a new language, the compile-time language package determines "what language the code can render", and the `base_language` data only determines "what languages ​​are enabled in the current deployment, how to sort them, and which language is the main language of dynamic resources".

## First understand the two levels of responsibilities

| Layer | Authoritative Source | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compilation period | Backend error directory, three-end core/System JSON, code generation directory | Language whitelist, fixed UI copywriting, error copywriting, code generation template |
| Runtime | `base_language` table | Language name, native name, enabled status, sorting, primary language |

Therefore, just adding a language record to the database cannot make the new language appear on the page; just adding front-end JSON cannot make the dynamic menu, dictionary and login page read the language. The two layers must be synchronized.

## Files to be added

Each language code must use the JSON file with the same name in the following seven language pack directories; the code generator also has a unified `catalog.json`:

| Table of Contents | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/internal/i18n/assets` | Backend Error Message Catalog |
| `frontend/admin/packages/core/src/locales` | Management base and public copy |
| `frontend/admin/packages/modules/system/src/locales` | Management System Copywriting |
| `frontend/uni-app/packages/core/src/locales` | uni-app base and public copy |
| `frontend/uni-app/packages/modules/system/src/locales` | uni-app System copywriting |
| `frontend/taro-app/packages/core/src/locales` | Taro base and public copy |
| `frontend/taro-app/packages/modules/system/src/locales` | Taro System Copywriter |
`backend/internal/biz/system/admin/codegen/locales/catalog.json` is not a language pack directory, but a code generator template and static terminology data organized by language code.

JSON keys, placeholders, and namespaces must remain unchanged. `common.language.<locale>` is used to display the language name offline and can be supplemented; the runtime name is read from the database first, so adding a new language does not require modifying the existing language package or TypeScript registration code.

## Key naming quick check

When adding fixed copy, first determine the module and component it belongs to, and then name it according to unified rules:

```text
前端：<模块>.<defineOptions.name 转换路径>.<文案类型>.<名称>
后端：<package 去掉版本>.<Service 转换路径>.<操作或对象>.<字段>.<规则>
```

Example:

```text
BaseDict -> system.base.dict.dialog.confirm_status
BaseDictService / system.admin.v1 -> system.admin.base.dict.create.name.required
CodeGenTable -> system.code.gen.table.field.page_type
```

The component name and service name are split into lowercase dot paths according to PascalCase; the end names, fields and rules use `snake_case`. Use `common.*` for cross-business public copy, and `common.error.*` for common back-end errors. The backend key does not contain `v1`; `message_key`. Renaming requires synchronization of Proto, Go and all language directories.

## Standard process

### 1. Select language code

uses the BCP 47 form, such as `de-DE`, `pt-BR`. The language code must be consistent in all directories, and two representations of `de` and `de-DE` cannot appear at the same time. The code needs to be parsable by Core's `resource/i18n` language resource directory, and the management side's Day.js and Element Plus locale dependencies can find the corresponding region or basic language mapping.

### 2. Add language pack

takes `zh-CN.json` as the key base, adds `<locale>.json` to the seven directories in the above table, and translates values ​​item by item:

```text
backend/internal/i18n/assets/de-DE.json
frontend/admin/packages/core/src/locales/de-DE.json
frontend/admin/packages/modules/system/src/locales/de-DE.json
frontend/uni-app/packages/core/src/locales/de-DE.json
frontend/uni-app/packages/modules/system/src/locales/de-DE.json
frontend/taro-app/packages/core/src/locales/de-DE.json
frontend/taro-app/packages/modules/system/src/locales/de-DE.json
```

The code generator's `catalog.json` is not split by file, but added to the same JSON object `"de-DE"`, fields must be kept intact: `menu`, `resource`, `password_strength`, `static`.

`common.language.<locale>` can be written to the management-side Core language package, used to display language names offline and generate `base_language` initial names for migration; runtime language names, sorting and enabling status are still subject to database records. Adding a new language does not require modifying the language name key in the existing language pack.

Placeholders such as `{name}`, `{field}`, `{max}`, `{{.Value}}` as well as URL, permission paths, dictionary code/value and HTML/Markdown tags must be preserved when translating. Do not translate routes `name`, `path`, `component` or API paths.

### 3. Run the synchronization script

Execute in the warehouse root directory:

```bash
make i18n-sync
```

script checks for:

- Whether the file sets in the seven language pack directories are consistent;
- Whether the key set and placeholders of each language pack are consistent;
- Whether the code generator language directory field is complete;
- Manages whether there are available mappings for Day.js and Element Plus.

After passing the check, the script generates the following files. Do not edit them manually:

- `src/locales/generated.ts` for six front-end packages;
- Management side Day.js, Element Plus locale mapping;
- `language.up.sql` and description files are generated when a migration version is passed in.

### 4. Generate database language records

The current warehouse uses `v0.0.1` for migration; this version is written when generating language initialization records:

```bash
make i18n-sync I18N_MIGRATION_VERSION=v0.0.1
```

script is only responsible for supplementing the `base_language` record. Using `INSERT IGNORE` will not overwrite the enabled status, sorting and main language configuration of the existing deployment. Check the migration version directory before submitting and ensure that `language.up.sql` is submitted together with the description file.

If the deployment does not want to enable the language immediately, you can adjust `base_language.status` to be disabled after migration; the main language can only be switched through the management side language configuration or database configuration, and cannot be changed through the front-end language package.

### 5. Prepare dynamic resource translation (optional)

Fixed UI and backend bugs Once the package is complete, new languages ​​can fall back to the main language at runtime. To provide fixed translations for built-in menus, dictionaries, dictionary items, and system configurations, you can use batch scripts to generate language packs and dynamic translation data:

```bash
I18N_OFFLINE=1 \
make i18n-locale I18N_LOCALE=de-DE
```

can be removed for online translation. `I18N_OFFLINE=1`. This command is written to the corresponding language package, `i18n.de-DE.up.sql` and description files under `v0.0.1` by default. Migration only writes non-empty fixed text, and existing values ​​will not be overwritten. If the language package has been manually completed, maintain `i18n.<locale>.up.sql` directly, and do not use this command to overwrite the manual translation.

Dynamic resources can also be edited in the management end internationalization maintenance page. The main language text with content in the form can be translated instantly individually or in batches. The Draft interface only returns a single translation and does not write it into the unified internationalization table; manual input will be directly saved to the unified internationalization table. Empty translations will enter the asynchronous internationalization queue after the resource is successfully created or updated. When submitting empty texts, they will also be filled in according to the save logic. Failure messages will be scanned again by the scheduled task, and existing non-empty translations will not be overwritten. The internationalization interface is only available when `I18N_DRAFT_ENABLED=true` or equivalent application metadata is enabled. The system configuration name and text and rich text type values ​​support internationalization. Pictures and Boolean values ​​are not sent out; when the runtime value is missing, it falls back to the main language.

### 6. Verify and submit

is recommended to be executed before submission:

```bash
make i18n-check
make i18n-sync
git diff --check

cd backend && go test ./...
cd ../frontend/admin && pnpm type:check && pnpm lint:oxlint
cd ../uni-app && pnpm tsc && pnpm lint
cd ../taro-app && pnpm tsc && pnpm lint
```

Confirm that the new language is available in the following scenarios: first startup, language switching before login, switching after login, refresh recovery, dynamic menu, dictionary display, verification error and main language fallback when dynamic translation is missing.

## Content that does not need to be modified

New languages ​​do not need to be modified:

- Go locale constants, backend service registration and error localization code;
- three-terminal locale runtime, module registration and request encapsulation;
- Proto, RPC makefiles and menu routing code.

These runtime files read the front-end registration files generated by compile-time language packs and synchronization scripts; the runtime enabled languages, default languages, and ordering are provided by the `base_language` database record. Only when a new language exposes that the basic library does not have locale mapping, the language package structure requires new fields, or the business does add a new translation key, corresponding dependencies or code changes are required.

## Troubleshooting

| Phenomenon | Check |
| --- | --- |
| `语言集合不一致` | Whether all seven language pack directories have the same name JSON |
| `语言键集合不一致` | Compare key and placeholder with same directory `zh-CN.json` |
| `代码生成器语言目录字段不完整` | `catalog.json` Whether it contains four fixed fields and complete subfields |
| `缺少组件语言映射` | Day.js/Element Plus Whether this region or base language file is provided |
| The language can be switched but the name is empty | Check the `base_language` record, or add `common.language.<locale>` |
| Menu/Dictionary still shows the main language | Check whether there is a non-empty record in the unified translation table, and whether the request is sent `Accept-Language` |

For the complete architecture description, see [Final Internationalization Plan] (国际化最终方案.md); for local constraints on the language pack directory, see the README of each directory.

documents.content:
# Interface parameter verification

The backend uses `buf.validate` to declare rules, and `backend/internal/server/middleware/validate.go` to call protovalidate in HTTP and gRPC business processing. When verification fails, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` is returned, and the response boundary is localized to `message` of the first violation according to the request language; the error reason and metadata remain stable.

The `rules` of the management side `ProForm` is used for real-time interactive prompts and cannot replace server-side verification; constraints at both ends should express the same business rules.

## Proto writing method

```proto
import "buf/validate/validate.proto";
import "gnostic/openapi/v3/annotations.proto";

message ExampleForm {
  string name = 1 [
    (gnostic.openapi.v3.property) = {description: "名称"},
    (buf.validate.field).cel = {
      id: "example.name.required"
      message: "请输入名称"
      expression: "this.size() > 0"
    },
    (buf.validate.field).cel = {
      id: "example.name.max_len"
      message: "名称不能超过 30 个字符"
      expression: "this.size() <= 30"
    }
  ]; // 名称
}

message CreateExampleRequest {
  ExampleForm example = 1 [
    (gnostic.openapi.v3.property) = {description: "示例表单"},
    (buf.validate.field).required = true
  ]; // 示例表单
}
```

The rule ID uses the stable `<resource>.<field>.<rule>`, and Chinese messages are directed to users. Don't rely on the generator's default English errors.

## Common rules

| Constraints | Proto |
| --- | --- |
| String required | CEL `this.size() > 0` |
| Maximum length | CEL `this.size() <= 30` |
| Positive ID | CEL `this > 0` |
| Required for nested messages | `(buf.validate.field).required = true` |
| Enumeration is legal | `(buf.validate.field).enum = {defined_only: true}` |
| The list is not empty | CEL `this.size() > 0` |
| Unique list | CEL `this.unique()` |
| Email | `(buf.validate.field).string.email = true` |
| URL | `(buf.validate.field).string.uri = true` |
| Regular | `(buf.validate.field).string.pattern = "..."` |
| Value collection | `(buf.validate.field).string.in = ["a", "b"]` |

Cross-field rules are written at the message level:

```proto
message PeriodForm {
  option (buf.validate.message).cel = {
    id: "period.range"
    message: "结束时间不能早于开始时间"
    expression: "this.end_at >= this.start_at"
  };

  int64 start_at = 1 [(gnostic.openapi.v3.property) = {description: "开始时间"}]; // 开始时间
  int64 end_at = 2 [(gnostic.openapi.v3.property) = {description: "结束时间"}]; // 结束时间
}
```

Uniqueness, foreign key existence, tenant permissions, protected resources and state transfer depend on the database or current identity, must be placed in biz, and cannot be disguised as format verification.

## ProForm corresponding

```ts
const fields: ProFormField[] = [
  {
    prop: "name",
    label: "名称",
    component: "input",
    props: { maxlength: 30, showWordLimit: true },
    rules: [
      { required: true, message: "请输入名称", trigger: "blur" },
      { max: 30, message: "名称不能超过 30 个字符", trigger: "blur" }
    ]
  }
];
```

- `required`, length, range, format and number of lists are provided on the front end.
- `maxlength`, `min`, `max` and other control restrictions should be consistent with rules and Proto.
- The business verification message returned by the backend is still the final result, and the frontend must not skip error processing just because it passes the form verification.
- `optional` Format rules are only executed when the field has a value; non-required fields on the front end should not add `required` unconditionally.

## Change check

1. Modify Proto annotation, OpenAPI description and `buf.validate`.
2. Execute `make -C backend api` and `make i18n-openapi`.
3. Execute `make -C backend ts-admin`, `make -C backend ts-uni-app` or `make -C backend ts-taro-app` according to the consumer side; execute `make -C backend ts` when three terminals need to be generated at one time.
4. Synchronize ProForm rules, control restrictions and interface error display.
5. Execute back-end testing and corresponding front-end type checking.

generates Go, OpenAPI, and TypeScript RPCs without manual modification.

# Database and initialization data

## Current data source

The system uses the MySQL database `kratos_admin` by default, and the configuration is located at `backend/configs/data.yaml` and `data_local.yaml`. Redis is used for caching status such as verification codes, one-time password keys, Tokens, etc.

`data.database` represents a single default data source; `data.databases` can declare multiple named data sources. The default data source saves system tables and `base_migration` execution records for all modules.

## Table creation and migration

The startup sequence is:

1. Create all GORM clients.
2. Execute `AutoMigrate` on the client to register the model.
3. Load module migration resources and execute `.up.sql` according to dependencies, versions, database types and data sources.
4. Complete OpenAPI interface data, tenant role menu and Casbin policy synchronization.

`enable_migrate` only controls GORM to automatically create tables and does not turn off versioned SQL. Fresh environments should enable it for the default data source, otherwise tables such as `base_migration` may not exist yet.

## Resource structure

Current built-in resources:

```text
backend/migration/assets/v0.0.1/mysql/
├── base_area.up.sql
├── default_data.up.sql
├── default_data.description.md
├── i18n.en-US.up.sql
├── i18n.zh-TW.up.sql
└── i18n.ja-JP.up.sql
```

directory rules:

```text
assets/<version>/<database-type>/<feature>.up.sql
assets/<version>/<database-type>/<feature>.down.sql          # 可选
assets/<version>/<database-type>/<feature>.description.md
assets/<version>/<database-type>/<data-source>/<feature>.up.sql
```

The current warehouse built and verified is `mysql`. The direct files in the database type directory belong to the `default` data source; the first-level subdirectory is the named data source and must be consistent with the configuration name. When you need to access other database types, you must first confirm the corresponding driver, model migration and SQL dialect, and then add a new migration directory. Scripts and descriptions are read sorted by file name.

The unique identifier of the migration record includes module, data source and version. Failure of any upgrade script within a version will roll back the version and prevent the service from starting. Restarting after repair will retry the unrecorded version.

## Initialization content

`default_data.up.sql` provides:

- Default tenant, department, position, role and `super`, `admin` development account.
- System configuration, dictionary, menu, button and service method permission relationship.
- Management side System page, AI, code generation, API documentation and application side required permissions entrance.

`default_data.up.sql` is responsible for language records, default business data, menus and permissions; the same version `i18n.{locale}.up.sql` provides non-primary language translations of menus, dictionaries, dictionary items and system configuration names/values ​​through `base_i18n.target_type`. The five types of translation data are written as single items `INSERT IGNORE`. The main language is configured by `base_language.is_primary`, the main table saves the main language text, and other enabled languages ​​​​are saved to the unified translation table. Translation table and code generation `i18n_config` field is created by GORM `AutoMigrate`.

`base_area.up.sql` provides basic regional data. Initialize SQL using `INSERT IGNORE`, skip when encountering an existing unique key record, and do not overwrite existing data.

On startup `BaseApiCase.InitializeOpenAPI` rebuilds the interface metadata based on the registered OpenAPI, then synchronizes the tenant admin menu and rebuilds the Casbin rules. Therefore, when modifying the Proto path or menu API list, you must also regenerate OpenAPI and update the versioned SQL.

## New environment

```sql
CREATE DATABASE kratos_admin CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
```

After starting the backend, the default development account is:

- `super / 112233`
- `admin / 112233`

These credentials are only used for local initialization and must be modified before deployment.

## Stock upgrade

- Do not modify the version directory that has been published and executed, and add a higher version.
- Structural changes, data fixes, menu and permission adjustments put in the same feature version.
- To add a new language, first press [International Language Expansion Guide] (国际化语言扩展指南.md) to generate the language package and `language.up.sql`; the dynamic fixed translation will also generate `i18n.<locale>.up.sql`.
- SQL remains idempotent, avoiding `TRUNCATE`, unconditional full table updates or deletes.
- Back up and verify rollback strategy before production execution; provide `.down.sql` explicitly when rollback is required.
