documents.content:
# Service access guide

This article explains how to integrate a new capability into the current Backend, Management or Application. Only describe the expansion methods that the warehouse has adopted.

## Determine ownership first

| Scenario | Backend Proto | Backend Implementation | Frontend |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shared by admin, uni-app and Taro | `api/proto/base/v1` | `biz/base`, `service/base/v1` | Three terminals generated and packaged on demand |
| System Administration | `api/proto/system/admin/v1` | `biz/system/admin`, `service/system/admin/v1` | System Module |
| Application system capabilities | `api/proto/system/app/v1` | `biz/system/app`, `service/system/app/v1` | uni-app and Taro |
| Independent business module | Module’s own Proto | Module’s own implementation | Independent management terminal, uni-app or Taro host module |

general types preferentially reuse `common.v1` in Buf; System cross-end enumeration puts `system/common/v1`.

## Built-in backend capabilities

1. When the table structure changes, update the development library first, and then run `make -C backend gorm-gen`.
2. Define Proto, HTTP mapping, OpenAPI description, and `buf.validate`.
3. Run `make -C backend api` and `make i18n-openapi`, according to the consumer side, run `make -C backend ts-admin`, `make -C backend ts-uni-app` or `make -C backend ts-taro-app`; run when three terminals need to be generated at one time `make -C backend ts`.
4. Implement the business in the corresponding `internal/biz/<proto-directory>`, and implement the Proto service in `internal/service/<proto-directory>`.
5. Add the service to the corresponding `internal/server/{base/v1,system/admin/v1,system/app/v1}/register.go`.
6. Update `backend/wire.go` after the ProviderSet or construction parameters change and run `make -C backend wire`.
7. Add default data, menu, button and service method permissions in the new migrated version.
8. If user-visible copy is added, synchronize the language package of the corresponding module and execute `make i18n-sync`.

The generated directories are `api/gen/go`, `internal/data/gen`, `internal/openapi/assets/openapi.yaml`, `src/rpc` and `wire_gen.go` for the management side, uni-app and Taro packages, and must not be edited manually.

service only does parameter passing, logging and error reporting; transactions, tenants, permissions and status rules are placed in biz; Repository uses the generated typed Query and does not splice runtime SQL.

## External Go module

The external module provides static resources that must be collected before building the business through `module.Resources`:

```go
func NewModuleResources() module.Resources {
	return module.Resources{
		ProjectKey:  "order",
		ProjectName: "订单",
		Models:      orderdata.Models(),
		OpenAPI:     orderopenapi.Assets(),
		Docs:        orderdocs.Assets(),
		Migrations: []module.Migration{{Name: "order", FS: ordermigration.Assets(), Path: "."}},
		I18n:        orderi18n.Assets(),
	}
}
```

Core will first initialize infrastructure such as databases, caches, and queues based on static resources. Then Wire builds modules Case and Service, and the complete module implements protocol registration and runtime contribution:

```go
type Module struct {
	service orderv1.OrderServiceHTTPServer
}

func (m *Module) RegisterHTTP(server *http.Server) {
	orderv1.RegisterOrderServiceHTTPServer(server, m.service)
}

func (m *Module) registerAI(registrar module.AIRegistrar) error {
	return registrar.RegisterTools(module.AITerminalAdmin, m.agentTools...)
}

func (m *Module) Contributions() module.Contributions {
	return module.Contributions{
		AI: m.registerAI,
		/* Tasks、SSE、StartupHooks */
	}
}
```

composition root uses `kratoscore.ProviderSet`, `kratoscore.BusinessProviderSet`, `NewModuleResources` and the module business Provider; Core is exposed through The `biz`, `biz/dto`, `config`, `module` types provide BaseCase, Job, SSE, OpenAPI and Docs capabilities, and the `internal` directory only retains Core implementation details.

Inter-module calls only use generated gRPC Clients. `Runtime.ClientConn()` is available in the process, the remote uses standard gRPC connection, and the calling code does not depend on Backend `internal`.

## Database and permissions

Migration directory:

```text
backend/migration/assets/vX.Y.Z/mysql/<feature>.up.sql
backend/migration/assets/vX.Y.Z/mysql/<feature>.description.md
backend/migration/assets/vX.Y.Z/mysql/<data-source>/<feature>.up.sql
```

The management menu `component` must use the complete module prefix, for example, the System page is `system/base/user/index`. Menu `api` saves the Proto service method identifier, such as `/system.admin.v1.BaseUserService/PageBaseUser`; the HTTP path is synchronized to `base_api` by OpenAPI. These two concepts cannot be mixed.

## Management module

The current default business module is `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system`:

```text
frontend/admin/packages/modules/system/src
├── api
├── rpc
├── views
├── module.ts
└── index.ts
```

pages are isolated by module name prefix:

```ts
const views = import.meta.glob<{ default: Component }>("./views/**/*.vue");

export const orderAdminModule = defineAdminModule({
  name: "order",
  views
});
```

`views/list/index.vue` corresponds to the menu component `order/list/index`. Modules can also declare `staticViews`, `headerTools`, `userMenuActions`, `routeOptions`, and name `extensions`.

The host maintains package names, loaders, and optional pre-built dependencies only in `apps/admin/src/module-manifest.ts`. When adding a module, the host `package.json` dependency is added simultaneously. Modules must not use core's private `@/*` path and may only reference the `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core` public subpath.

Create an independent business workspace in this warehouse:

```bash
cd frontend/admin
pnpm module:create ../../../order-admin --module order
```

## Application host

The application-side page is placed in `src/views` of the package it belongs to, and the physical page and stable view key are declared through the module's `pages` and `views`. The request is placed in `src/api` of the package it belongs to. The business type comes from the generated `src/rpc`. The page does not directly call `uni.request`.

External hosts can use:

```ts
const result = bootstrapKratosApp({
  app: App,
  pinia,
  modules: [{
    name: "order",
    pages: { "pagesOrder/list/index": {} },
    views: { ORDER_LIST: "pagesOrder/list/index" }
  }]
});
```

`KratosAppModule` describes the module page using `pages`, `views`, and optionally `icons`. The `@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core/vite` of the release package exposes `kratosApp()` and `createKratosUniPlugin()`; the external host passes the same module list in the Vite configuration to reuse page scanning, wrapper generation, static resource merging and post-build recovery capabilities.

The access example of this warehouse is located at `frontend/uni-app/apps/uni-app/vite.config.ts`. The same path page is subject to the host configuration. The later registration module can overwrite the first registration module.

The Taro host uses `defineKratosTaroModule()` and `defineKratosTaroBuildModule()` to declare runtime, page and build-time entries simultaneously. The configuration example is located at `frontend/taro-app/apps/taro-app/src/module-manifest.ts`. Module pages are assembled by `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-core/runner` during build, the host does not commit the generated wrapper or page configuration.

## Verify

```bash
make i18n-check
cd backend && go test ./...
pnpm --dir frontend/admin check:exports
pnpm --dir frontend/admin lint:oxlint
pnpm --dir frontend/admin type:check
pnpm --dir frontend/uni-app test
```

# Login and password encryption

This article records the account password, verification code, OAuth, password ciphertext and Token mechanism currently shared by the management end, uni-app and Taro. The interface is based on `backend/api/proto/base/v1/login.proto`, `oauth.proto`.

## Log in with account and password

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant UI as 前端
  participant API as Backend
  participant Cache as Redis
  UI->>API: GET /api/v1/base/config
  UI->>API: GET /api/v1/base/captcha
  UI->>API: POST /api/v1/base/captcha/verify（行为验证码）
  UI->>API: GET /api/v1/base/password-public-key?scene=LOGIN
  API->>Cache: 保存一次性私钥，TTL 5 分钟
  UI->>UI: RSA-OAEP + AES-GCM 加密密码
  UI->>API: POST /api/v1/base/session
  API->>Cache: 消费验证码和一次性私钥
  API-->>UI: access_token / refresh_token / expires_in
  UI->>API: GET 当前端 profile
```

When the tenant code is not passed, the backend uses the default tenant. The account is queried by `tenant_code + user_name`; there is currently no branch logged in by the independent `phone` field.

Ordinary verification code submits `captcha_id` and the user's answer directly. Verification codes for behaviors such as sliders, clicks, and rotations first call `/api/v1/base/captcha/verify` to obtain a one-time `captcha_token` valid for 2 minutes, and then submit the token as the login `captcha_code`.

## Password protocol

algorithm identification:

```text
RSA-OAEP-256+A256GCM
```

1. The front end requests the one-time RSA public key of the specified scenario.
2. The front end performs `trim()` on the password, generating a 32-byte AES-256 key and a 12-byte GCM IV.
3. AES-GCM encryption password, RSA-OAEP(SHA-256) encryption AES key.
4. Submit `key_id`, `nonce`, `algorithm`, `encrypted_key`, `iv`, `ciphertext` after Base64 encoding.
5. Backend verification scenario, nonce and algorithm, read and immediately delete the private key from Redis, decrypt it and compare the database password hash with `go-utils/crypto.Verify`.

One-time key has a TTL of 5 minutes and is deleted once read. The same ciphertext cannot be replayed; if a retry fails, the public key must be retrieved and encrypted again.

H5 on the management side and both application sides uses Web Crypto. uni-app and Taro WeChat mini programs use `asmcrypto.js`, `wx.getRandomValues` and WeChat Base64 API statically introduced by their respective bases to avoid dynamic import compatibility issues in the mini program environment.

## WeChat Mini Program OAuth

Application side `MP-WEIXIN` uses provider `wechatmini`:

1. `wx.login()` Get code and submit `/api/v1/base/oauth/session`.
2. Return Token directly when it is bound or automatic registration is allowed.
3. When not bound, `binding_required=true` is returned, and the page displays the tenant, user name, password and verification code.
4. Call `wx.login()` again before binding submission, and then request `/api/v1/base/oauth/binding/session`.

WeChat code can only be used once, and the same code cannot be reused for detection of binding status and formal binding.

The management side also supports OAuth provider list, authorization jump, callback, binding list and unbinding; the specific provider is configured by `backend/configs/oauth*.yaml`.

## Token

login response contains `token_type`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and `expires_in`. The front end saves `Bearer <access_token>`, refresh token and the converted absolute expiration time.

The application request layer calls `POST /api/v1/base/token` when the access token remains no more than 5 minutes, and concurrent refreshes share the same Promise. The backend issues a new access token and retains the original refresh token. If the refresh fails, the local login status will be cleared; logging out will delete the access/refresh token and the cached authentication information corresponding to the refresh token.

Public authentication requests use `authMode: "none"` or equivalent configuration, and do not carry the old `Authorization`; requests that require login automatically add Token.

## Key entry

| realm | path |
| --- | --- |
| Login Proto | `backend/api/proto/base/v1/login.proto` |
| OAuth Proto | `backend/api/proto/base/v1/oauth.proto` |
| Backend login | `backend/internal/biz/base/login.go` |
| Backend OAuth | `backend/internal/biz/base/oauth.go` |
| Key generation and decryption | `backend/internal/biz/base/utils/password_crypto.go` |
| Management side password encryption | `frontend/admin/packages/core/src/utils/passwordCrypto.ts` |
| uni-app login and password encryption | `frontend/uni-app/packages/core/src/views/pages/login/login.vue`, `frontend/uni-app/packages/core/src/utils/passwordCrypto.ts` |
| Taro login and password encryption | `frontend/taro-app/packages/core/src/views/pages/login/login.tsx`, `frontend/taro-app/packages/core/src/utils/passwordCrypto.ts` |
| Application-side Token and request | Each of the two application-side `packages/core/src/utils/auth.ts`, `http.ts` |

When troubleshooting login failure, check the configuration, verification code, public key, ciphertext scenario, login response, token saving and profile request in sequence. Do not record clear text passwords, private keys, full tokens, or verification code answers in logs or documents.

# Overall system design

This article only describes the modules, running relationships and expansion boundaries that already exist in the current warehouse. See [docs/README](README.md) for the document entry. The specific commands are subject to the README and Makefile of each module.

## module

| Module | Responsibilities | Products |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | Kratos HTTP/gRPC service, authentication authority, system business, AI, tasks, migration and static hosting. | Go services, OpenAPI |
| `kratos-core` | Reusable Kratos host runtime without business proto. | Standalone Go module |
| `frontend/admin/packages/core` | Management side startup, login, dynamic routing, layout, status and public components. | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core` |
| `frontend/admin/packages/modules/system` | System management, personal center, AI and development tool pages. | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system` |
| `frontend/admin/packages/cli` | Create business management end workspace. | `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli` |
| `frontend/admin/apps/admin` | The default management host that combines core and System. | Private package `@liujitcn/kratos-admin`, `backend/data/admin` |
| `frontend/uni-app` | Home, Login, My, Profile, Settings, WebView and AI uni-app application. | `@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app`, `backend/data/app` |
| `frontend/taro-app` | A React/Taro application that shares the backend contract with uni-app and supports H5 and WeChat applets. | `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app`, `backend/data/app` |
| `backend/migration` | Versioned database and initialization data. | Embedded SQL |

The warehouse currently does not have business modules such as shopping mall, order, payment, recommendation, etc.

## Running relationship

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Admin["管理端宿主"] -->|"/api /events"| Backend["Backend"]
  UniApp["uni-app"] -->|"/api"| Backend
  Taro["Taro app"] -->|"/api"| Backend
  Backend --> DB[("MySQL")]
  Backend --> Redis[("Redis")]
  Backend -->|"/admin/"| AdminFiles["data/admin"]
  Backend -->|"/app/"| AppFiles["data/app"]
  Module["外部 core.Module"] --> Backend
```

Backend can run independently or can be connected to other Core hosts through `kratosadmin.NewModule`. The two forms reuse the same Service, biz and Repository; in-process calls use `Runtime.ClientConn()`, and remote calls use standard gRPC connections.

## Backend layering

```text
api/proto
  -> api/gen/go
  -> internal/service/{base/v1,system/admin/v1,system/app/v1}
  -> internal/biz/{base,system/admin,system/app,...}
  -> internal/data/gen
```

- Proto is the only contract source for HTTP, gRPC, checksum frontend types.
- service only does transmission adaptation and error reporting, business rules are placed in biz, and database access is limited to data.
- `internal/server/{base/v1,system/admin/v1,system/app/v1}` registers the transmission service; `internal/module` is responsible for the module adaptation from Admin to Core and the Wire combination root. The root directory `wire.go` only provides a public assembly facade, and `internal/cmd` is responsible for the process startup entrance.
- Cross-module data access only using generated clients, does not expose internal Model, Query, Repository or Case.

Core's `Module` is responsible for gRPC, HTTP, MCP registration; optional Contributor can provide middleware, background server, OpenAPI, tasks, queue consumers, SSE, startup scripts, startup hooks, health checks and static resources.

## Front-end boundary

The management side dependency direction is fixed to:

```text
apps/admin -> packages/modules/system -> packages/core
```

Business modules provide module-prefixed pages, static page replacements, top tools, user menus, routing options, and named extensions via `AdminModule`. The default host's module list is maintained only in `apps/admin/src/module-manifest.ts`.

The application side is an independent pnpm workspace, and the dependency direction is fixed as:

```text
apps/uni-app -> packages/modules/system -> packages/core
```

`KratosAppModule` declares pages, stable view keys, and static icons via `pages`, `views`, and `icons`. The host only maintains `apps/uni-app/src/module-manifest.ts`, and the Vite plug-in exposed by core scans the module page and merges `pages.json` and static resources during the build period.

The Taro application uses an independent React/Taro workspace, and the dependency direction is:

```text
apps/taro-app -> packages/modules/* -> packages/ui -> packages/core
```

`defineKratosTaroModule()` declares the runtime module, `defineKratosTaroBuildModule()` provides a build-time page description; the runner of `packages/core` generates page wrappers, subcontracting configurations and static resources during development or build, and the host only submits fixed bootstrap pages.

## Contract and generation

| Command | Output |
| --- | --- |
| `make -C backend api` | `backend/api/gen/go` |
| `make i18n-openapi` | `backend/internal/openapi/assets/openapi.yaml`, `openapi.en-US.yaml`, `openapi.zh-TW.yaml`, `openapi.ja-JP.yaml` |
| `make -C backend ts-admin` | `src/rpc` of management core and system |
| `make -C backend ts-uni-app` | `src/rpc` of uni-app core and system packages |
| `make -C backend ts-taro-app` | `src/rpc` of Taro core and system packages |
| `make -C backend ts` | Generate management, uni-app and Taro all at once `src/rpc` |
| `make -C backend gorm-gen` | `backend/internal/data/gen` |
| `make -C backend wire` | `backend/wire_gen.go` |

The interface change is completed by "Proto → Generate → service/biz → Front-end request and page → Migrate permissions". The generated files do not need to be modified manually.

## Data and permissions

Migration resources are organized by `assets/<version>/<database-type>/<data-source?>`. The default MySQL resource is located at `backend/migration/assets/v0.0.1/mysql`. At startup, GORM automatically builds tables according to configuration, then executes versioned SQL, and finally synchronizes `base_api`, tenant role menu and Casbin policy from OpenAPI and menu relationships.

uses JWT access/refresh token for authentication; password transmission uses one-time RSA-OAEP + AES-GCM hybrid encryption; tenant and permissions are determined by the server.

## Document index

| Topics | Documentation |
| --- | --- |
| Backend and Core | [backend README](../backend/README.md), standalone `kratos-core` repository |
| Management | [frontend/admin README](../frontend/admin/README.md) |
| Application | [frontend/uni-app README](../frontend/uni-app/README.md) |
| Taro application | [frontend/taro-app README](../frontend/taro-app/README.md) |
| New capability access | [Service access guide](服务接入指南.md) |
| Database | [Database and initialization data design](数据库与初始化数据设计.md) |
| Interface verification | [Interface parameter verification design](接口参数校验设计.md) |
| Login | [Login and password encryption process](登录与密码加密流程.md) |
| AI | [AI assistant design](AI助手设计.md) |
| Management-side components | [Front-end component list](前端组件清单.md) |
| International Design | [Final Internationalization Plan](国际化最终方案.md) |
| New languages | [International Language Extension Guide](国际化语言扩展指南.md) |

# frontend/admin

The management background uses pnpm workspace, organized by "thin host + core base + optional business modules + engineering tools". The host is only responsible for combination and startup; pages, requests, RPC types and business dependencies belong to the corresponding module package.

dependency direction is fixed to `app -> business module -> core`. The core does not depend on any business modules, and business modules do not reference each other by default; when reuse is really needed, they can only use the Interface exposed by the other party's `package.json#exports`.

## Directory Responsibilities

```text
frontend/admin
├── apps/admin                        # 装配当前全部 module 的默认宿主
├── packages/core                     # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-core 底座
│   ├── src/api/{base,system}         # 按 Proto 领域组织的底座请求
│   ├── src/components                # 公共组件
│   ├── src/layouts                   # 布局
│   ├── src/modules                   # 模块注册 interface
│   ├── src/rpc                       # 登录、菜单和底座能力 Proto 类型
│   └── src/views                     # 登录与静态错误页面
├── packages/modules/system           # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-system
│   └── src/{api,rpc,views}           # API 与 RPC 按 Proto 领域层级维护
├── packages/cli                      # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli
│   └── templates/business-workspace  # 完整 pnpm workspace 模板
├── internal/vite-config              # 当前仓库宿主构建配置
├── internal/tsconfig                 # 共享 TypeScript 配置
├── internal/lint-config              # 共享 Oxlint 配置
├── scripts/build-package.mjs          # core 与业务模块的 npm 发布构建器
├── package.json                       # workspace 命令与公共开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── tsconfig.json                      # workspace TypeScript 路径映射
└── turbo.json
```

`apps/admin/src/module-manifest.ts` is the only source of default host module configuration, and declares the runtime loader, Vite scanning package and pre-built dependencies; `apps/admin/src/modules.ts` loads and exports all modules of the current host by default. Core's business view directory only retains the login page. 403, 404, 500, and Pending are provided by core with default static implementations; the personal center, AI assistant, and system management pages are all provided by `systemAdminModule`. The personal center and AI assistant dynamically register routes through the backend menu and do not declare static business routes in the host.

## Root directory file

| path | function |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/` | A collection of runnable management hosts; the current default host is `admin`.                  |
| `packages/core/` | Publishable admin runtime, layouts, components and base pages.                      |
| `packages/modules/` | A collection of optional business modules, APIs and pages are maintained together within the module.                    |
| `packages/cli/` | Publishable standalone business workspace command line tool and template.                     |
| `internal/` | Vite, TypeScript and lint configuration packages only for use by the current source code repository.          |
| `scripts/build-package.mjs` | Generate a copy of the npm package source code and TypeScript declaration, and convert the core internal source code alias. |
| `package.json` | Declare workspace-level commands, tool dependencies, Node and pnpm versions.              |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Fixed dependency resolution results for the entire workspace.                               |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | Declare the workspace package under `apps`, `packages`, and `internal`.         |
| `tsconfig.json` | Inherit the shared configuration and declare the source code path mapping of this warehouse.                            |
| `turbo.json` | Defines development, build, release build, and type checking task relationships.                      |
| `AGENTS.md` | Collaboration and code constraints of the management directory.                                      |
| `.editorconfig` | General editor indentation, newline and character set rules.                                |
| `.gitignore` | The management-side local product ignores the rules.                                          |
| `.oxlintignore` | Oxlint scan exclusion rules.                                             |
| `.prettierignore`, `.prettierrc.cjs` | Prettier exclusion range and format configuration.                                     |
| `.stylelintignore`, `.stylelintrc.cjs` | Stylelint exclude scope and style rules.                                    |
| `lint-staged.config.cjs` | Management-side temporary file check configuration used by warehouse-level Git hook.                    |
| `commitlint.config.cjs` | Git submission information verification rules.                                            |
| `postcss.config.cjs` | PostCSS and browser prefix handling configuration.                                    |
| `README.md` | workspace architecture, public commands and module access instructions.                          |

Each subdirectory containing `package.json` has a sibling `README.md`, which describes the package's internal file and directory responsibilities.

The management side publishes `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core`, `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system` and
`@liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli`. The default host `@liujitcn/kratos-admin` is a private package and cannot be entered.
npm packaging and distribution manifest.

## Development and Construction

```bash
cd frontend/admin
pnpm install
pnpm dev
pnpm check:exports
pnpm test
pnpm type:check
pnpm lint:oxlint
pnpm build
pnpm build:package
```

In the `frontend/admin` directory, you can also execute common processes through the upper-level Makefile:

```bash
make -C .. run-admin
make -C .. check-admin
make -C .. build-admin
make -C .. package-admin
```

The default host address is `http://localhost:8848`. The environment variable is located in `apps/admin/.env*`, the development mode API agent and the production build output directory are managed uniformly by the host Vite configuration; the current production build is written to `backend/data/admin`.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by the management side are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The language keys and placeholder sets are verified when registering the module. The login page and the top toolbar share the locale store. Switching languages ​​does not refresh the page, and retains the current routing, query parameters and unsubmitted forms.

The language preference is saved as `kratos-admin:locale`. Axios, refresh token, native fetch, SSE and Swagger requests are uniformly sent to `Accept-Language`; dynamic menus and dictionaries are returned by the backend by locale, and fall back to the main language when the current language translation is missing. To add a new language, you need to synchronize the back-end error directory, the six front-end language package directories of the three workspaces, and code generation `catalog.json`, and then execute `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory; the registration file and Day.js mapping are generated by the script. For the specific process, see [International Language Expansion Guide](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md).

API is organized into directories such as `api/base`, `api/system` according to Proto first-level fields; RPC retains complete Proto levels such as `rpc/base/v1`, `rpc/system/admin/v1`. RPC types are placed according to real consumer ownership: core retains login, menu, user information and service types required during startup capabilities; System self-contained system management, personal center, AI and its dependency types. After modifying Proto, execute `make ts-admin` in `backend`. The command will clean and generate RPCs for core and system according to two Buf configurations respectively; execute `make ts` when you need to generate three front-end RPCs at one time. When the server-side contract has not completed fine-grained splitting, the same generated file may temporarily contain methods that are not called by the current package, and the generated file is not manually written.

The core internal source code uses `@/*`; the business module uses `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/*` and its own package name. Vue Router is used for page jumps between modules, and cross-directory relative references are prohibited for code reuse.

root TypeScript path and host Vite source code alias only map the entry declared by `package.json#exports` for each npm package. The `@/*` used internally by the core implementation is retained due to source code transfer compilation, but `pnpm check:exports` will scan imports in applications, core, business modules and internal build configurations, and reject undisclosed subpaths, non-core `@/*` references and business module cross-package relative references; warehouse-level pre-commit will first process the temporary files and then execute core Dependency direction and package export bounds checking.

## module interface

core exports `bootstrapAdminApp`, `defineAdminModule`, the view registry, and the top tools, user menu, and routing behavior extensions. The business module entrance declares the name and page loader to access the dynamic page:

```ts
import type { Component } from "vue";
import { defineAdminModule } from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core";

const views = import.meta.glob<{ default: Component }>("./views/**/*.vue");

export const orderAdminModule = defineAdminModule({
  name: "order",
  views
});
```

business page only registers the module prefix path, so `views/list/index.vue` is uniformly parsed by `order/list/index`, and the `list/index` unprefixed alias is not provided. The `component` of the backend menu must write the complete module path; even if different modules contain `views` pages with the same name, they will not cover each other. The host declares the module in `src/module-manifest.ts`, `src/modules.ts` loads and exports all modules by default, and the Vite build configuration is derived from the manifest:

```ts
export const adminModuleManifest = [
  {
    packageName: "@order/admin-module",
    load: async () => (await import("@order/admin-module")).orderAdminModule
  }
];
```

### Replace static page

core exposes the fixed view keys of all static pages through `ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS`:

| Properties | View Keys |
| -------------- | --------------- |
| `LOGIN` | `login/index` |
| `FORBIDDEN` | `error/403` |
| `NOT_FOUND` | `error/404` |
| `SERVER_ERROR` | `error/500` |
| `PENDING` | `error/pending` |

The business module explicitly maps any of its pages to fixed view keys through `staticViews`, and the later registration module replaces the first registration implementation:

```ts
import { ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS, defineAdminModule } from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core";

export const orderAdminModule = defineAdminModule({
  name: "order",
  staticViews: {
    [ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS.NOT_FOUND]: () => import("./components/NotFound.vue"),
    [ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS.PENDING]: () => import("./components/Pending.vue")
  }
});
```

Normal `views` is always isolated by module name, only `staticViews` is replaceable Seam. The npm Interface of core only exposes module access, component whitelist, and stable entrances such as `request`, `navigation`, `table`, `security`, `stores/runtime`; business modules must not rely on the internal source code path of core.

## Create business project

The business project generated by CLI itself is also a pnpm workspace, including an independent host and a publishable business module package:

```bash
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli create shop-admin --module shop
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli create shop-admin --module shop,order

# 当前仓库开发
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop,order
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop --module order
```

generates results:

```text
shop-admin
├── apps/admin
│   └── README.md
├── packages/modules/shop
│   └── README.md
├── packages/modules/order
│   └── README.md
├── scripts/build-package.mjs
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── README.md
├── tsconfig.json
└── turbo.json
```

CLI imports `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system` by default first, and then imports and creates its own module according to the `--module` parameter sequence. `--module` is reusable and also accepts comma-separated names; `--with` only adds additional published modules to the host portfolio, without creating their source code or creating implicit dependencies between business modules. The CLI refuses to overwrite an existing directory.

# frontend/taro-app

`frontend/taro-app` is a standalone pnpm workspace that implements the same application functionality and vision as `frontend/uni-app` in React 18 and Taro 4. Currently supports H5 and WeChat mini programs, including home page, login, agreement, WebView, personal center, settings, personal information and AI assistant, but does not include mall, order, payment or recommendation services.

## Workspace

```text
frontend/taro-app
├── apps/taro-app                 # 私有 Taro 宿主，不发布
├── packages/core                 # 运行时、基础页面和构建 runner
├── packages/ui                   # NutUI 主题与按需图标适配
├── packages/modules/system       # 个人中心、设置、资料和 AI
├── packages/cli                  # 独立 workspace 脚手架
├── scripts                       # package exports 边界检查
├── package.json                  # 公共命令和开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml           # workspace 包范围
└── turbo.json                    # 跨包任务依赖
```

The dependency direction is fixed to:

```text
apps/taro-app -> packages/modules/* -> packages/ui -> packages/core
```

core does not depend on UI or business modules; system only provides reuse capabilities through the core and UI's public exports; the host is only responsible for combining modules and platform configuration.

Detailed description:

- [Private Host](apps/taro-app/README.md)
- [Application Base](packages/core/README.md)
- [UI Basic Package](packages/ui/README.md)
- [system module](packages/modules/system/README.md)
- [Project Scaffolding](packages/cli/README.md)

## Page assembly

`apps/taro-app/src/module-manifest.ts` is a unique module manifest, and the order of declaration determines the override priority for pages, stable `viewKey` and icons. The module declares runtime capabilities through `defineKratosTaroModule()` and exposes the build-time page description through `defineKratosTaroBuildModule()`.

The host only submits fixed `pages/bootstrap` pages. The core runner completes the following operations before development or build begins:

- Scan each module for `src/views/**/*.tsx`, ignoring `components` at any level.
- Generate page wrapper and page config, mount the self-drawn `KratosTabBar` in a unified manner, and complete the top bar consistent with uni-app for the H5 default navigation page.
- Split main package and sub-package by `pages*` root directory.
- Merge each module `src/static` to the host. Priority will be given to existing files on the host, and priority will be given to files with the same name as modules registered.
- Restore the original `app.config.ts` after the build exits and delete the temporary file.

The page wrapper is mounted and self-drawn in a unified manner `KratosTabBar`; the fixed home page and my page are registered as hidden native tab routes at the same time, and `switchTab` is used when switching to maintain the native effect of WeChat, dynamically expand the tab and then reuse the page stack. Ordinary pages use `navigateTo` first, and subordinate pages will belong along the parent relationship and highlight the corresponding tab.

All `Taro.request`, file uploads, and SSE requests are sent uniformly to `Accept-Language`. The dynamic menu follows the title parsed by the backend, and falls back to the main language when the current language translation is missing; adding a new language requires synchronizing the backend error directory, the six front-end language pack directories of the three workspaces and code generation `catalog.json`, and then executing `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory. ```

```bash

pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create shop-app --module shop,order
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create my-app --with @acme/customer-module
```

- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-ui`

# frontend/uni-app

`frontend/uni-app` is an independent pnpm workspace that provides directly runnable uni-app host, publishable application base, system business module and project scaffolding. The technology stack is `uni-app + Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite + Pinia + Sass`, currently supporting H5 and WeChat applets.

The application side only reuses the layering idea of ​​the management side and does not rely on the source code or workspace of `frontend/admin`. Currently, the home page, login, agreement, WebView, personal center, settings, personal information and AI assistant are retained, and the mall, order, payment or recommendation services are not included.

## Workspace

```text
frontend/uni-app
├── apps
│   └── uni-app                # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app，默认宿主，不发布
│       ├── src
│       │   ├── pages/bootstrap
│       │   ├── module-manifest.ts
│       │   ├── manifest.json
│       │   └── pages.json
│       ├── README.md
│       └── package.json
├── packages
│   ├── core                   # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core v0.0.17
│   │   ├── src                # 底座运行时、页面、状态和构建插件
│   │   ├── test
│   │   ├── README.md
│   │   └── package.json
│   ├── modules
│   │   └── system             # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-system v0.0.17
│   │       ├── src            # 个人中心、设置和 AI
│   │       ├── README.md
│   │       └── package.json
│   └── cli                    # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-cli v0.0.17
│       ├── bin
│       ├── src
│       ├── test
│       ├── README.md
│       └── package.json
├── scripts                    # 包导出边界检查
├── README.md                  # workspace 总览和公共命令
├── package.json               # workspace 脚本与公共开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml        # workspace 包范围
└── turbo.json                 # 跨包任务依赖与缓存配置
```

The dependency direction is fixed to:

```text
@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app
  -> @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-system
  -> @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core
```

- `core` Responsible for authentication, requests, configuration, Pinia, base pages, status pages, dynamic navigation and building plugins.
- `system` is responsible for the personal center, information, settings and AI pages, and only reuses base capabilities through the public exports of `core`.
- `apps/uni-app` only maintains the host entry, manifest, module list, bootstrap page and Vite configuration.
- `cli` creates a separate pnpm workspace with the same structure.

For the directory boundaries, functions and public entries of each package, see:

- [Host Application](apps/uni-app/README.md)
- [Application Base](packages/core/README.md)
- [system module](packages/modules/system/README.md)
- [Project Scaffolding](packages/cli/README.md)

workspace root directory no longer retains the `src`, `bin` or empty template directory of the old single application. The business source code can only be located in the corresponding host or package.

## Page assembly

The host maintains a unique module list in `apps/uni-app/src/module-manifest.ts`, and the order determines the static view override priority:

```ts
export const moduleManifest = [coreModule, systemModule]
```

Each module is declared using `defineKratosAppModule()`:

- `pages`: Page styling and optional physical routing overrides.
- `views`: Stable mapping of `viewKey` to physical pages.
- `icons`: In-module icons that can be referenced by dynamic navigation.

The build plug-in automatically scans the `src/views/**/*.vue` of each module and ignores the `components` directory at any level. Post-registration modules can replace the previous module's static pages with the same physical route or `viewKey`.

hosts `pages.json` which only submits fixed bootstrap pages. During development or construction, the plug-in will temporarily generate page wrappers, merge page configurations, and merge module static files into the host file by file; host files with the same name are given priority, and transactions only record and clean files actually written by the plug-in. Automatically resumes after exiting normally. If the process is forcibly terminated, the previous transaction will be restored based on `.kratos-uni-app-pages-state.json` the next time it is started. The same host allows only one H5 or applet development/building process to hold page transactions at the same time. The current process needs to be stopped before switching platforms.

## Dynamic navigation

The default menu interface is consistent with the management side `base-menu` service:

```text
GET /api/v1/app/base/menu
```

requests the service path to `/v1/app/base/menu`, which is spliced ​​by the unified `/api` base. `base_menu.id = 999` is the hidden fixed root directory of the mobile terminal. The backend queries the enablement page below it layer by layer and maintains a flat response. Core then presses `parent_id` to build the menu tree; you can also access the compatibility contract through `setAppNavigationAdapter()`. The root directory is only associated with mobile menu queries, and each page menu is associated with the protected API actually called by the page.

Menu configuration constraints:

- `path` uses `app/` prefix, supports `:参数` and query.
- `name` Use the `App` prefix.
- The title and main icon use `meta.title`, `meta.icon`, the icon can use an HTTPS address or a key registered in the module `icons`.
- The mobile terminal configuration is placed in `meta.app` without adding independent table fields.
- `meta.app.view_key` must have been registered by the module, and the interface cannot directly deliver any component path.
- `meta.app.access` supports `PUBLIC`, `GUEST_ONLY`, `AUTHENTICATED`, which is semantically consistent with the management-side login permissions.
- The secondary page of the root directory is fixed as a tab. The homepage uses `99901`, mine uses `99909`, and `99902` to `99908` are reserved for business tabs.
- `meta.app.in_tab_bar` of the second-level tab is fixed to true, and the number can only be 0 or 2–5 items; the selected icon uses `meta.app.selected_icon`, and the lower-level page is fixed to non-tab.

The management menu form recursively identifies the entire mobile terminal tree of `999`, displays the logical path, logical name, view key, access mode, mobile terminal icon and API permissions of the page; automatically sets tabs according to the level when submitting, and uniformly packages the mobile terminal configuration into the existing `meta.app`.

Navigation configuration is cached separately in anonymous state and login state. The new configuration will be fully verified and then switched atomically; if the remote end fails, the last successful cache of the current identity will be used; if there is no cache, the local default menu will be used.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by uni-app are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The key and placeholder set are verified when registering the module; login, home page, status page, WebView, personal center, settings, information and AI pages all use fixed copy through `t(key)`. The language preference is saved as `kratos-app:locale`, and the stable routing and business fields will not be changed after switching.

All `uni.request`, file uploads, and SSE requests are sent uniformly to `Accept-Language`. The dynamic menu follows the title parsed by the backend, and falls back to the main language when the current language translation is missing; adding a new language requires synchronizing the backend error directory, the six front-end language pack directories of the three workspaces and code generation `catalog.json`, and then executing `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory. For the specific process, see [International Language Expansion Guide](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md).

The page wrapper is mounted and self-drawn in a unified manner `KratosTabBar`; the fixed home page and my page are registered as hidden native tab routes at the same time, and `switchTab` is used when switching to maintain the native effect of WeChat, dynamically expand the tab and then reuse the page stack. Ordinary pages use `navigateTo` first, and subordinate pages will belong along the parent relationship and highlight the corresponding tab. Therefore, the menu level, logical path and `viewKey` can be adjusted after the interface content changes, without having to write each business route in the host.

## Development and Construction

```bash
cd frontend/uni-app
pnpm install

pnpm dev:h5
pnpm dev:mp-weixin
```

The upper-level Frontend Makefile provides the corresponding aggregation entry:

```bash
make -C .. run-uni-app      # 微信小程序开发
make -C .. check-uni-app
make -C .. build-uni-app    # H5 构建
make -C .. package-uni-app
```

development and build commands are guaranteed to be executed first by `turbo.json`; independent testing and

`http://localhost:7001`.
The root command is scheduled by Turbo according to the workspace dependency graph; core and

```bash

pnpm build:mp-weixin
```

- H5 products are written to `backend/data/uni-app`, and the backend is mounted through `/uni-app/`.
- WeChat applet product is written into `apps/uni-app/dist/build/mp-weixin` and imported using WeChat developer tools.

## RPC generation

```bash
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-cli create my-app --with @acme/pay
```

- Includes system module by default.
- `--module` creates local modules in the workspace.
- `--with` Add published module dependencies.
- Refuse to overwrite if target directory already exists.
- `README.md` is generated in the workspace root directory, `apps/uni-app` and each local module, ensuring that each
`package.json` has the same level directory structure and function description.

The generated host contains the Vue 3 `createSSRApp` entry, module manifest, bootstrap page, manifest, Vite configuration, TypeScript configuration and H5 HTML.
